controls.title: Ensure cramfs kernel module is not available
controls.description: Checks that the cramfs kernel module (a compressed read-only filesystem for embedded devices) cannot be used: it is either absent, or unloaded, deny-listed and mapped to a disabled install command.
controls.rationale: Kernel code that the system never needs still enlarges its attack surface; making the module unloadable removes it as an attack path.
controls.business_impact: An attacker who can present crafted a compressed read-only filesystem for embedded devices content could trigger automatic loading of cramfs and exploit a driver flaw to crash the host or gain kernel privileges.
controls.recommendation: Disable the cramfs module unless a documented business need requires it.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf containing 'install cramfs /bin/false' and 'blacklist cramfs', then unload it with 'modprobe -r cramfs'.

controls.title: Ensure /tmp is tmpfs or a separate partition
controls.description: Checks that /tmp is its own mount (a tmpfs or a separate partition) and tmp.mount is not masked or disabled.
controls.rationale: A dedicated /tmp filesystem contains resource exhaustion and allows restrictive mount options for the data it holds.
controls.business_impact: If /tmp fills up it can exhaust the root filesystem, and restrictive mount options such as nodev, nosuid and noexec cannot be applied to it.
controls.recommendation: Mount /tmp as a separate filesystem.
controls.remediation: Debian 13 mounts /tmp as a tmpfs through tmp.mount: run 'systemctl unmask tmp.mount' and 'systemctl enable tmp.mount', or add an /etc/fstab entry for /tmp.

controls.title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
controls.description: Checks that /tmp, when it is a separate mount, is mounted with nodev, which blocks device files on it.
controls.rationale: /tmp does not need device files, so the nodev option removes an avenue for abuse at no functional cost.
controls.business_impact: Device files created on this filesystem could give direct access to disks or kernel memory.
controls.recommendation: Mount /tmp with the nodev option.
controls.remediation: Add nodev to the options of the /tmp entry in /etc/fstab (or to a systemd mount override for /tmp), then run 'mount -o remount /tmp'.

controls.title: Ensure nosuid option set on /tmp partition
controls.description: Checks that /tmp, when it is a separate mount, is mounted with nosuid, which blocks setuid and setgid programs on it.
controls.rationale: /tmp does not need setuid and setgid programs, so the nosuid option removes an avenue for abuse at no functional cost.
controls.business_impact: A setuid program placed on this filesystem could be used to escalate privileges.
controls.recommendation: Mount /tmp with the nosuid option.
controls.remediation: Add nosuid to the options of the /tmp entry in /etc/fstab (or to a systemd mount override for /tmp), then run 'mount -o remount /tmp'.

controls.title: Ensure weak dependencies are configured
controls.description: Checks that APT does not automatically install recommended or suggested packages.
controls.rationale: Installing only explicitly requested packages keeps the software inventory minimal and reviewable.
controls.business_impact: Weak dependencies silently add software, services and code paths that nobody chose to deploy or maintain.
controls.recommendation: Configure APT to install only hard dependencies.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/60-cis-weak-deps containing 'APT::Install-Recommends "0";' and 'APT::Install-Suggests "0";'.

controls.title: Ensure access to gpg key files are configured
controls.description: Checks that APT keyring files in /usr/share/keyrings, /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d and any Signed-By location are root-owned and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Repository signing keys decide which packages the system trusts.
controls.business_impact: A user who can modify a trusted keyring can make the system accept and install attacker-signed packages as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict APT keyring files to root ownership and mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <keyring>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <keyring>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d directory is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0755.
controls.rationale: /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d holds trusted repository signing keys; only root should be able to add or replace entries in it.
controls.business_impact: A writable /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d lets an unprivileged user change which repositories or credentials APT uses, leading to installation of malicious packages.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d to root ownership and mode 0755 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d' and 'chmod 0755 /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/apt/auth.conf.d directory is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/apt/auth.conf.d is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0755.
controls.rationale: /etc/apt/auth.conf.d holds repository login credentials; only root should be able to add or replace entries in it.
controls.business_impact: A writable /etc/apt/auth.conf.d lets an unprivileged user change which repositories or credentials APT uses, leading to installation of malicious packages.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/apt/auth.conf.d to root ownership and mode 0755 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/apt/auth.conf.d' and 'chmod 0755 /etc/apt/auth.conf.d'.

controls.title: Ensure access to files in the /etc/apt/auth.conf.d/ directory is configured
controls.description: Checks that files in /etc/apt/auth.conf.d are root-owned and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: These files contain credentials for authenticated package repositories.
controls.business_impact: Readable repository credentials can be reused to access private package feeds or pivot into the software supply chain.
controls.recommendation: Restrict repository credential files to root with mode 0640 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/apt/auth.conf.d/*' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/apt/auth.conf.d/*'.

controls.rationale: /etc/apt/sources.list.d holds repository definitions; only root should be able to add or replace entries in it.
controls.business_impact: A writable /etc/apt/sources.list.d lets an unprivileged user change which repositories or credentials APT uses, leading to installation of malicious packages.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/apt/sources.list.d to root ownership and mode 0755 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/apt/sources.list.d' and 'chmod 0755 /etc/apt/sources.list.d'.

controls.title: Ensure access to files in /etc/apt/sources.list.d are configured
controls.description: Checks that repository definition files in /etc/apt/sources.list.d are root-owned and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Repository definitions determine where packages are downloaded from.
controls.business_impact: A user who can edit a repository file can redirect package installation to an attacker-controlled mirror.
controls.recommendation: Restrict repository definition files to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*'.

controls.title: Ensure repositories are set to https in /etc/apt/sources.list
controls.description: Checks that no repository in /etc/apt/sources.list uses plain HTTP.
controls.rationale: HTTPS protects package metadata and downloads from eavesdropping and tampering in transit, complementing signature checks.
controls.business_impact: Over HTTP an on-path attacker can observe which packages are installed and attempt downgrade or freeze attacks against the package metadata.
controls.recommendation: Use HTTPS repository URIs.
controls.remediation: Change 'http://' URIs in /etc/apt/sources.list to 'https://' (for example https://deb.debian.org/debian) and run 'apt update'.

notes.proxmox: The Proxmox VE documentation configures the no-subscription and Ceph repositories as http://download.proxmox.com; APT still verifies them through signed Release files. Switch them to https:// where the mirror supports it, or record an exception.

controls.title: Ensure repositories are set to https in /etc/apt/sources.list.d directory
controls.description: Checks that no repository in /etc/apt/sources.list.d uses plain HTTP.
controls.rationale: HTTPS protects package metadata and downloads from eavesdropping and tampering in transit, complementing signature checks.
controls.business_impact: Over HTTP an on-path attacker can observe which packages are installed and attempt downgrade or freeze attacks against the package metadata.
controls.recommendation: Use HTTPS repository URIs.
controls.remediation: Change 'http://' URIs in /etc/apt/sources.list.d to 'https://' (for example https://deb.debian.org/debian) and run 'apt update'.

notes.proxmox: The Proxmox VE documentation configures the no-subscription and Ceph repositories as http://download.proxmox.com; APT still verifies them through signed Release files. Switch them to https:// where the mirror supports it, or record an exception.

controls.title: Ensure AllowInsecureRepositories is configured
controls.description: Checks that Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories is explicitly set to "0" in the APT configuration.
controls.rationale: Unsigned repositories bypass APT's package authentication. Explicit configuration prevents a later configuration file from silently changing the behaviour.
controls.business_impact: Allowing unsigned repositories lets an attacker who controls a mirror or the network deliver arbitrary packages.
controls.recommendation: Set Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories to "0" explicitly.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/60-cis-allowinsecurerepositories containing 'Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories "false";' and remove conflicting settings.

controls.title: Ensure AllowWeakRepositories is configured
controls.description: Checks that Acquire::AllowWeakRepositories is explicitly set to "0" in the APT configuration.
controls.rationale: Weakly signed repositories rely on broken digest or signature algorithms. Explicit configuration prevents a later configuration file from silently changing the behaviour.
controls.business_impact: Weak signatures can be forged, allowing tampered package metadata to be accepted.
controls.recommendation: Set Acquire::AllowWeakRepositories to "0" explicitly.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/60-cis-allowweakrepositories containing 'Acquire::AllowWeakRepositories "false";' and remove conflicting settings.

controls.title: Ensure AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories is configured
controls.description: Checks that Acquire::AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories is explicitly set to "0" in the APT configuration.
controls.rationale: A signed repository must never be downgraded to an unsigned one. Explicit configuration prevents a later configuration file from silently changing the behaviour.
controls.business_impact: A downgrade lets an attacker strip signatures from a previously trusted repository and serve malicious packages.
controls.recommendation: Set Acquire::AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories to "0" explicitly.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/60-cis-allowdowngradetoinsecurerepositories containing 'Acquire::AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories "false";' and remove conflicting settings.

controls.title: Ensure Acquire::Check-Date is configured
controls.description: Checks that Acquire::Check-Date is explicitly set to "1" in the APT configuration.
controls.rationale: Date checks reject stale or future-dated Release files. Explicit configuration prevents a later configuration file from silently changing the behaviour.
controls.business_impact: Without date validation, replayed old metadata can keep the system on vulnerable package versions.
controls.recommendation: Set Acquire::Check-Date to "1" explicitly.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/60-cis-check-date containing 'Acquire::Check-Date "true";' and remove conflicting settings.

controls.title: Ensure apparmor packages are installed
controls.description: Checks that the apparmor and apparmor-utils packages are installed.
controls.rationale: AppArmor provides mandatory access control that confines services beyond ordinary file permissions.
controls.business_impact: Without AppArmor a compromised service can use every privilege of its Unix account instead of a narrow profile.
controls.recommendation: Install AppArmor and its management utilities.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install apparmor apparmor-utils'.

controls.title: Ensure AppArmor is enabled
controls.description: Checks that AppArmor is not disabled on the kernel command line, that apparmor.service is enabled and active, and that profiles are loaded.
controls.rationale: Mandatory access control only protects the system when it is enforced at boot and at runtime.
controls.business_impact: With AppArmor disabled, every confined service runs unconfined, so a single exploited daemon has far wider access to files and capabilities.
controls.recommendation: Enable AppArmor at boot and keep its profiles loaded.
controls.remediation: Remove apparmor=0 from GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX and /etc/default/grub.d/apparmor.cfg, run 'update-grub', then 'systemctl enable --now apparmor'.

controls.title: Ensure all AppArmor Profiles are enforcing
controls.description: Checks that every loaded AppArmor profile is in enforce mode and that no process with a defined profile runs unconfined.
controls.rationale: Profiles in complain mode only log violations; they do not block them.
controls.business_impact: Services whose profiles are not enforced can perform actions their profile would deny, so an exploit is not contained.
controls.recommendation: Enforce all AppArmor profiles after validating them.
controls.remediation: Run 'aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/*' after testing, develop real rules for stub profiles, and restart processes reported as unconfined.

controls.title: Ensure kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined is enabled
controls.description: Checks that kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined is 1 at runtime and in the sysctl configuration.
controls.rationale: The setting stops unprivileged, unconfined processes from changing into less restricted AppArmor profiles.
controls.business_impact: Without it an unprivileged attacker can escape AppArmor restrictions, for example to reach unprivileged user namespaces.
controls.recommendation: Enable kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined.
controls.remediation: Add 'kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf and run 'sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1'.

controls.title: Ensure bootloader password is set
controls.description: Checks that GRUB defines a superuser protected by a PBKDF2 password hash.
controls.rationale: A bootloader password stops console users from editing boot entries or passing kernel parameters.
controls.business_impact: Anyone with console access could boot into single-user mode or add init=/bin/bash and obtain a root shell without credentials.
controls.recommendation: Protect the GRUB configuration with a superuser password.
controls.remediation: Generate a hash with 'grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2', add 'set superusers="<user>"' and 'password_pbkdf2 <user> <hash>' to /etc/grub.d/40_custom, then run 'update-grub'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE installed on ZFS with UEFI boots through systemd-boot (managed by proxmox-boot-tool), where GRUB settings do not apply; there, protect the boot process with a firmware (UEFI) setup password and Secure Boot.

controls.title: Ensure access to bootloader config is configured
controls.description: Checks that /boot/grub/grub.cfg is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0600.
controls.rationale: The GRUB configuration contains boot parameters and may contain password hashes.
controls.business_impact: Readable or writable bootloader configuration exposes password hashes for offline cracking and allows boot parameters to be altered.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the GRUB configuration to root with mode 0600.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /boot/grub/grub.cfg' and 'chmod u-x,go-rwx /boot/grub/grub.cfg' (repeat after update-grub regenerates it).

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE installed on ZFS with UEFI boots through systemd-boot (managed by proxmox-boot-tool), where GRUB settings do not apply; there, protect the boot process with a firmware (UEFI) setup password and Secure Boot.

controls.title: Ensure fs.protected_hardlinks is configured
controls.description: Checks that fs.protected_hardlinks is 1 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Hard-link protection stops users from creating links to files they do not own.
controls.business_impact: Without it an attacker can exploit time-of-check/time-of-use races in privileged programs through crafted hard links.
controls.recommendation: Set fs.protected_hardlinks to 1 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'fs.protected_hardlinks = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w fs.protected_hardlinks=1'.

controls.title: Ensure fs.protected_symlinks is configured
controls.description: Checks that fs.protected_symlinks is 1 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Symlink protection restricts following symlinks in world-writable sticky directories.
controls.business_impact: Without it a local attacker can plant symlinks in /tmp to trick privileged processes into overwriting arbitrary files.
controls.recommendation: Set fs.protected_symlinks to 1 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'fs.protected_symlinks = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w fs.protected_symlinks=1'.

controls.title: Ensure kernel.yama.ptrace_scope is configured
controls.description: Checks that kernel.yama.ptrace_scope is 1 or 2 or 3 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Yama restricts which processes may attach to others with ptrace.
controls.business_impact: With unrestricted ptrace, any compromised process can read the memory of other processes owned by the same user, including credentials and keys.
controls.recommendation: Set kernel.yama.ptrace_scope to 1 or 2 or 3 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1'.

controls.title: Ensure fs.suid_dumpable is configured
controls.description: Checks that fs.suid_dumpable is 0 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Setuid programs should not produce core dumps.
controls.business_impact: Core dumps of privileged programs can contain password hashes, keys and other secrets readable from disk.
controls.recommendation: Set fs.suid_dumpable to 0 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'fs.suid_dumpable = 0' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=0'.

controls.title: Ensure kernel.dmesg_restrict is configured
controls.description: Checks that kernel.dmesg_restrict is 1 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Restricting the kernel log to privileged users limits information disclosure.
controls.business_impact: Kernel messages reveal addresses and hardware details that help attackers tune kernel exploits.
controls.recommendation: Set kernel.dmesg_restrict to 1 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w kernel.dmesg_restrict=1'.

controls.title: Ensure prelink is not installed
controls.description: Checks that prelink is not installed.
controls.rationale: prelink modifies binaries in place, which defeats address randomization and file integrity monitoring.
controls.business_impact: Prelinked binaries weaken ASLR and cause integrity tools such as AIDE to report changes that hide real tampering.
controls.recommendation: Remove prelink.
controls.remediation: Run 'prelink -ua' to restore binaries, then 'apt purge prelink'.

controls.title: Ensure Automatic Error Reporting is configured
controls.description: Checks that the Apport automatic error reporting service is not enabled or running.
controls.rationale: Crash reports can capture memory contents of the crashing process.
controls.business_impact: Automatically collected crash reports may contain credentials or personal data and have historically been abused for local privilege escalation.
controls.recommendation: Disable automatic error reporting.
controls.remediation: Set 'enabled=0' in /etc/default/apport and run 'systemctl --now disable apport', or remove the apport package.

controls.title: Ensure kernel.kptr_restrict is configured
controls.description: Checks that kernel.kptr_restrict is 1 or 2 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Hiding kernel pointers from unprivileged users limits information disclosure.
controls.business_impact: Exposed kernel addresses defeat kernel address randomization and simplify kernel exploits.
controls.recommendation: Set kernel.kptr_restrict to 1 or 2 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'kernel.kptr_restrict = 1' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w kernel.kptr_restrict=1'.

controls.title: Ensure kernel.randomize_va_space is configured
controls.description: Checks that kernel.randomize_va_space is 2 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: Full address space layout randomization places stacks, heaps and libraries at unpredictable addresses.
controls.business_impact: Without ASLR, memory-corruption exploits against any service become far more reliable.
controls.recommendation: Set kernel.randomize_va_space to 2 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'kernel.randomize_va_space = 2' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=2'.

controls.title: Ensure core file size is configured
controls.description: Checks that a hard core file size limit of 0 applies to all users ('* hard core 0') and that no entry allows larger core files.
controls.rationale: Preventing core dumps keeps process memory, which may hold secrets, from being written to disk.
controls.business_impact: Core files can expose passwords, keys and session tokens held in the memory of crashing programs.
controls.recommendation: Set a hard core size limit of 0 for all users.
controls.remediation: Add '* hard core 0' to a file such as /etc/security/limits.d/60-cis.conf and remove entries that allow core files.

controls.title: Ensure systemd-coredump ProcessSizeMax is configured
controls.description: Checks that systemd-coredump sets ProcessSizeMax=0 (compliant automatically when systemd-coredump is not installed).
controls.rationale: systemd-coredump should neither process nor store core dumps on production systems.
controls.business_impact: Stored core dumps can disclose secrets from process memory and consume disk space.
controls.recommendation: Set ProcessSizeMax=0 for systemd-coredump.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/60-cis.conf containing '[Coredump]' and 'ProcessSizeMax=0', then run 'systemctl daemon-reload'.

controls.title: Ensure systemd-coredump Storage is configured
controls.description: Checks that systemd-coredump sets Storage=none (compliant automatically when systemd-coredump is not installed).
controls.rationale: systemd-coredump should neither process nor store core dumps on production systems.
controls.business_impact: Stored core dumps can disclose secrets from process memory and consume disk space.
controls.recommendation: Set Storage=none for systemd-coredump.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/60-cis.conf containing '[Coredump]' and 'Storage=none', then run 'systemctl daemon-reload'.

controls.title: Ensure /etc/motd is configured
controls.description: Checks that the message of the day (/etc/motd and /etc/motd.d) contains no \m, \r, \s or \v escape sequences and no reference to the operating system name.
controls.rationale: Login banners should state authorized-use terms without disclosing the operating system or kernel version.
controls.business_impact: Banners that reveal the OS name and version help attackers select exploits and fingerprint the host before authenticating.
controls.recommendation: Replace the message of the day (/etc/motd and /etc/motd.d) with an authorized-use notice that does not identify the platform.
controls.remediation: Edit or remove /etc/motd and files in /etc/motd.d so they contain only site-approved text.

controls.title: Ensure /etc/issue is configured
controls.description: Checks that the local login banner (/etc/issue and issue.d) contains no \m, \r, \s or \v escape sequences and no reference to the operating system name.
controls.rationale: Login banners should state authorized-use terms without disclosing the operating system or kernel version.
controls.business_impact: Banners that reveal the OS name and version help attackers select exploits and fingerprint the host before authenticating.
controls.recommendation: Replace the local login banner (/etc/issue and issue.d) with an authorized-use notice that does not identify the platform.
controls.remediation: Write the approved notice to /etc/issue, for example: echo 'Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored and reported.' > /etc/issue.

controls.title: Ensure /etc/issue.net is configured
controls.description: Checks that the remote login banner (/etc/issue.net) contains no \m, \r, \s or \v escape sequences and no reference to the operating system name.
controls.rationale: Login banners should state authorized-use terms without disclosing the operating system or kernel version.
controls.business_impact: Banners that reveal the OS name and version help attackers select exploits and fingerprint the host before authenticating.
controls.recommendation: Replace the remote login banner (/etc/issue.net) with an authorized-use notice that does not identify the platform.
controls.remediation: Write the approved notice to /etc/issue.net, for example: echo 'Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored and reported.' > /etc/issue.net.

controls.title: Ensure pam_motd is configured
controls.description: Checks that every file shown by pam_motd (motd= in the sshd, login, su and gdm-password PAM stacks) contains no \m, \r, \s or \v escape sequences and no reference to the operating system name.
controls.rationale: Login banners should state authorized-use terms without disclosing the operating system or kernel version.
controls.business_impact: Banners that reveal the OS name and version help attackers select exploits and fingerprint the host before authenticating.
controls.recommendation: Replace every file shown by pam_motd (motd= in the sshd, login, su and gdm-password PAM stacks) with an authorized-use notice that does not identify the platform.
controls.remediation: Edit the files referenced by motd= in /etc/pam.d, or disable the dynamic MOTD scripts in /etc/update-motd.d that write system details to /run/motd.dynamic.

controls.title: Ensure sshd warning Banner is configured
controls.description: Checks that the file configured as the sshd Banner contains no \m, \r, \s or \v escape sequences and no reference to the operating system name.
controls.rationale: Login banners should state authorized-use terms without disclosing the operating system or kernel version.
controls.business_impact: Banners that reveal the OS name and version help attackers select exploits and fingerprint the host before authenticating.
controls.recommendation: Replace the file configured as the sshd Banner with an authorized-use notice that does not identify the platform.
controls.remediation: Point Banner at an approved notice file (for example /etc/issue.net) and remove OS details from it, then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

check.missing_message: sshd has no Banner file configured, so no warning banner is shown before SSH authentication.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/motd is configured
controls.description: Checks that every MOTD file (including /etc/update-motd.d scripts, which CIS expects to be non-executable) is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Only root should be able to change the text presented to users at login.
controls.business_impact: A writable banner lets an unprivileged user alter legal notices or display misleading instructions to other users.
controls.recommendation: Restrict every MOTD file (including /etc/update-motd.d scripts, which CIS expects to be non-executable) to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <file>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <file>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/issue is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/issue and the issue.d files is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Only root should be able to change the text presented to users at login.
controls.business_impact: A writable banner lets an unprivileged user alter legal notices or display misleading instructions to other users.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/issue and the issue.d files to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <file>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <file>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/issue.net is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/issue.net is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Only root should be able to change the text presented to users at login.
controls.business_impact: A writable banner lets an unprivileged user alter legal notices or display misleading instructions to other users.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/issue.net to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <file>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <file>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure access to pam_motd file is configured
controls.description: Checks that every file referenced by pam_motd motd= arguments is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Only root should be able to change the text presented to users at login.
controls.business_impact: A writable banner lets an unprivileged user alter legal notices or display misleading instructions to other users.
controls.recommendation: Restrict every file referenced by pam_motd motd= arguments to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <file>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <file>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure access to sshd warning banner is configured
controls.description: Checks that the sshd Banner file is owned by root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Only root should be able to change the text presented to users at login.
controls.business_impact: A writable banner lets an unprivileged user alter legal notices or display misleading instructions to other users.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the sshd Banner file to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root <file>' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx <file>' for each reported file.

controls.title: Ensure update-notifier-motd.service is not in use
controls.description: Checks that update-notifier-motd.service is neither enabled nor active (compliant when update-notifier-common is not installed, the Debian 13 default).
controls.rationale: Dynamic MOTD update notices reveal patch status to anyone who logs in.
controls.business_impact: Announcing pending updates tells an attacker which vulnerabilities are likely still present.
controls.recommendation: Disable update-notifier-motd.service.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl --now mask update-notifier-motd.service' or remove update-notifier-common.

controls.title: Ensure update-notifier-motd.timer is not in use
controls.description: Checks that update-notifier-motd.timer is neither enabled nor active (compliant when update-notifier-common is not installed, the Debian 13 default).
controls.rationale: Dynamic MOTD update notices reveal patch status to anyone who logs in.
controls.business_impact: Announcing pending updates tells an attacker which vulnerabilities are likely still present.
controls.recommendation: Disable update-notifier-motd.timer.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl --now mask update-notifier-motd.timer' or remove update-notifier-common.

controls.title: Ensure GDM login banner is configured
controls.description: Checks that the GDM login banner is enabled with approved text, and that each setting is locked system-wide.
controls.rationale: A warning banner at the graphical login states the terms of authorized use.
controls.business_impact: Without a banner the organization weakens its legal position when prosecuting or disciplining misuse.
controls.recommendation: Enable and lock an approved GDM login banner.
controls.remediation: Add banner-message-enable=true and banner-message-text='<notice>' under [org/gnome/login-screen] in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/, lock both keys in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks/, and run 'dconf update'.

controls.title: Ensure GDM disable-user-list is configured
controls.description: Checks that the GDM user list is disabled, and that each setting is locked system-wide.
controls.rationale: Hiding the user list forces users to type their user name.
controls.business_impact: A visible user list discloses valid account names to anyone at the console, halving the work of password guessing.
controls.recommendation: Disable and lock the GDM user list.
controls.remediation: Add disable-user-list=true under [org/gnome/login-screen] in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/, lock it in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks/, and run 'dconf update'.

controls.title: Ensure GDM screen lock is configured
controls.description: Checks that the screen locks after at most 15 minutes of inactivity and within 5 seconds of blanking, and that each setting is locked system-wide.
controls.rationale: Automatic screen locking protects unattended sessions.
controls.business_impact: An unlocked, unattended session gives anyone nearby the logged-in user's access.
controls.recommendation: Configure and lock an idle screen lock of 15 minutes or less.
controls.remediation: Set idle-delay=uint32 900 under [org/gnome/desktop/session] and lock-delay=uint32 5 under [org/gnome/desktop/screensaver] in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/, lock both keys, and run 'dconf update'.

controls.title: Ensure GDM automount is configured
controls.description: Checks that GNOME automount of removable media is disabled, and that each setting is locked system-wide.
controls.rationale: Removable media should only be mounted deliberately.
controls.business_impact: Automatic mounting exposes filesystem drivers to untrusted media and eases introduction of malware or data theft.
controls.recommendation: Disable and lock GNOME automount.
controls.remediation: Set automount=false and automount-open=false under [org/gnome/desktop/media-handling] in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/, lock both keys, and run 'dconf update'.

controls.title: Ensure GDM autorun-never is configured
controls.description: Checks that GNOME autorun of removable media is disabled, and that each setting is locked system-wide.
controls.rationale: Software on removable media should never run automatically.
controls.business_impact: Autorun lets malicious media execute code as soon as it is inserted.
controls.recommendation: Disable and lock GNOME autorun.
controls.remediation: Set autorun-never=true under [org/gnome/desktop/media-handling] in /etc/dconf/db/local.d/, lock the key, and run 'dconf update'.

controls.title: Ensure XDMCP is not enabled
controls.description: Checks that XDMCP is not enabled in the GDM configuration.
controls.rationale: XDMCP sends graphical login sessions, including credentials, over the network without encryption.
controls.business_impact: Credentials and session contents can be captured on the network, and the display manager is exposed to remote attack.
controls.recommendation: Disable XDMCP.
controls.remediation: Remove 'Enable=true' from the [xdmcp] section of /etc/gdm3/custom.conf and /etc/gdm3/daemon.conf.

controls.title: Ensure Xwayland is configured
controls.description: Checks that GDM sets WaylandEnable=false in its [daemon] configuration, as CIS prescribes for Xwayland.
controls.rationale: CIS recommends a single, known display-server configuration for GDM.
controls.business_impact: An unmanaged display-server stack increases the graphical attack surface exposed through the display manager.
controls.recommendation: Set WaylandEnable=false for GDM.
controls.remediation: Add 'WaylandEnable=false' under [daemon] in /etc/gdm3/custom.conf and restart GDM during a maintenance window.

controls.title: Ensure autofs services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the automounter (autofs) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that autofs.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: autofs mounts filesystems, including removable media and network shares, on demand.
controls.business_impact: Automatic mounting lets users introduce untrusted media and exposes filesystem drivers to crafted content.
controls.recommendation: Remove the automounter unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge autofs'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask autofs.service'.

controls.title: Ensure avahi daemon services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Avahi mDNS/DNS-SD daemon (avahi-daemon) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that avahi-daemon.socket, avahi-daemon.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Avahi advertises and discovers services on the local network.
controls.business_impact: Service advertisements disclose host details and the daemon adds a network listener that has had remote vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Avahi mDNS/DNS-SD daemon unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge avahi-daemon'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask avahi-daemon.socket avahi-daemon.service'.

controls.title: Ensure dhcp server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Kea DHCP server (kea) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that kea-dhcp-ddns-server.service, kea-dhcp4-server.service, kea-dhcp6-server.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: A DHCP server is only needed on hosts that assign network configuration.
controls.business_impact: A rogue or exposed DHCP service can redirect clients to attacker-controlled gateways and DNS servers.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Kea DHCP server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge kea'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask kea-dhcp-ddns-server.service kea-dhcp4-server.service kea-dhcp6-server.service'.

controls.title: Ensure dns server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the BIND DNS server (bind9) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that named.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: A DNS server is only needed on hosts that provide name resolution.
controls.business_impact: An unmanaged DNS server can be abused for amplification attacks or cache poisoning and adds a remotely reachable service.
controls.recommendation: Remove the BIND DNS server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge bind9'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask named.service'.

controls.title: Ensure dnsmasq services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the dnsmasq DNS/DHCP service (dnsmasq) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that dnsmasq.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: dnsmasq provides DNS and DHCP services that most servers do not need.
controls.business_impact: dnsmasq has had remotely exploitable vulnerabilities and can hand out malicious network settings.
controls.recommendation: Remove the dnsmasq DNS/DHCP service unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge dnsmasq'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask dnsmasq.service'.

controls.title: Ensure ftp server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the FTP server (vsftpd) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that vsftpd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: FTP transfers data and, unless wrapped in TLS, credentials in clear text.
controls.business_impact: FTP credentials and files can be intercepted on the network, and anonymous or misconfigured FTP exposes data.
controls.recommendation: Remove the FTP server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge vsftpd'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask vsftpd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure ldap server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the OpenLDAP server (slapd) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that slapd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: An LDAP directory server is only needed on directory hosts.
controls.business_impact: An unmanaged directory service can disclose account data or accept unauthorized changes.
controls.recommendation: Remove the OpenLDAP server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge slapd'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask slapd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure message access server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the IMAP/POP3 server (dovecot-imapd, dovecot-pop3d) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that dovecot.socket, dovecot.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Mail access services are only needed on mail servers.
controls.business_impact: An exposed mail access service invites password guessing and may accept clear-text logins.
controls.recommendation: Remove the IMAP/POP3 server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge dovecot-imapd dovecot-pop3d'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask dovecot.socket dovecot.service'.

controls.title: Ensure network file system services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the NFS server (nfs-kernel-server) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that nfs-server.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: NFS exports filesystems to other hosts.
controls.business_impact: Mis-scoped NFS exports expose data and can allow file changes from other hosts with weak authentication.
controls.recommendation: Remove the NFS server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge nfs-kernel-server'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask nfs-server.service'.

controls.title: Ensure nis server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the NIS server (ypserv) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that ypserv.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: NIS is an obsolete directory protocol with no meaningful authentication or encryption.
controls.business_impact: NIS maps, including password hashes, can be retrieved by any host that can reach the server.
controls.recommendation: Remove the NIS server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge ypserv'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask ypserv.service'.

controls.title: Ensure print server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the CUPS print server (cups) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that cups.socket, cups.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Printing services are rarely needed on servers.
controls.business_impact: CUPS adds a network-facing service that has had remote code execution vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Remove the CUPS print server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge cups'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask cups.socket cups.service'.

controls.title: Ensure rpcbind services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the rpcbind portmapper (rpcbind) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that rpcbind.socket, rpcbind.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: rpcbind maps RPC services to ports and is only needed for NFS and other RPC services.
controls.business_impact: rpcbind discloses RPC services, can be abused for reflection attacks and widens the remote attack surface.
controls.recommendation: Remove the rpcbind portmapper unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge rpcbind'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask rpcbind.socket rpcbind.service'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE needs rpcbind when the node mounts NFSv3 storage; keep it only where NFS storage is configured and restrict it with the Proxmox VE firewall.

controls.title: Ensure rsync services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the rsync daemon (rsync) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that rsync.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: The rsync daemon serves files over an unencrypted protocol; rsync over SSH does not need it.
controls.business_impact: An rsync daemon can expose or accept files without strong authentication or encryption.
controls.recommendation: Remove the rsync daemon unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge rsync'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask rsync.service'.

controls.title: Ensure samba file server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Samba file server (samba) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that smbd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: SMB file sharing is only needed on file servers.
controls.business_impact: Samba is a frequent target of remote exploits and misconfigured shares expose data.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Samba file server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge samba'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask smbd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure snmp services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the SNMP agent (snmpd) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that snmpd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: SNMP exposes system information for monitoring and older versions authenticate with clear-text community strings.
controls.business_impact: Default or weak community strings disclose detailed configuration and may allow configuration changes.
controls.recommendation: Remove the SNMP agent unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge snmpd'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask snmpd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure telnet server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Telnet server (^telnetd) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that inetutils-inetd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Telnet transmits sessions, including credentials, in clear text.
controls.business_impact: Anyone on the network path can capture Telnet credentials and hijack sessions.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Telnet server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge ^telnetd'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask inetutils-inetd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure tftp server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the TFTP server (tftpd-hpa) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that tftpd-hpa.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: TFTP has no authentication and is only needed for network boot services.
controls.business_impact: Any host that can reach TFTP can read (and possibly write) the files it serves.
controls.recommendation: Remove the TFTP server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge tftpd-hpa'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask tftpd-hpa.service'.

controls.title: Ensure web proxy server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Squid web proxy (squid) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that squid.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: A web proxy is only needed on dedicated proxy hosts.
controls.business_impact: An unmanaged proxy can be abused to relay attacks or bypass network egress controls.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Squid web proxy unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge squid'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask squid.service'.

controls.title: Ensure web server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the web server (apache2, nginx) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that apache2.socket, apache2.service, nginx.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Web servers should only run on hosts whose role is to serve web content.
controls.business_impact: An unmanaged web server adds a remotely reachable service and may expose default content or files.
controls.recommendation: Remove the web server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge apache2 nginx'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask apache2.socket apache2.service nginx.service'.

controls.title: Ensure xinetd services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the xinetd super-server (xinetd) is not installed or, when another package requires it, that xinetd.service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: xinetd starts legacy network services on demand.
controls.business_impact: Legacy services started by xinetd are often insecure and easy to overlook.
controls.recommendation: Remove the xinetd super-server unless it is required and approved.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge xinetd'; if a dependency requires the package, run 'systemctl --now mask xinetd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure X window server services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the X Window System server (xserver-common) is not installed on a server.
controls.rationale: Servers rarely need a graphical display server.
controls.business_impact: The X server is large, runs with elevated privileges and adds local attack surface without serving a business purpose.
controls.recommendation: Remove the X Window System from servers.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge xserver-common' after confirming no graphical workloads depend on it.

controls.title: Ensure mail transfer agents are configured for local-only mode
controls.description: Checks that nothing listens on SMTP ports 25, 465 or 587 on a non-loopback address and that the MTA is configured for local-only delivery.
controls.rationale: Servers usually only need to send mail, not accept it from the network.
controls.business_impact: A network-reachable MTA can be abused as an open relay or exploited remotely.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the mail transfer agent to the loopback interface.
controls.remediation: For Postfix set 'inet_interfaces = loopback-only' in /etc/postfix/main.cf and restart postfix; for Exim run 'dpkg-reconfigure exim4-config' and choose local delivery on 127.0.0.1 and ::1.

controls.title: Ensure nis client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the NIS client (nis) is not installed.
controls.rationale: The NIS client depends on an insecure, obsolete directory protocol.
controls.business_impact: NIS clients trust unauthenticated directory data, allowing account spoofing on the network.
controls.recommendation: Remove the NIS client.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge nis'.

controls.title: Ensure rsh client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the rsh client (rsh-client) is not installed.
controls.rationale: rsh, rcp and rlogin authenticate by host name and send data in clear text.
controls.business_impact: rsh sessions can be intercepted or spoofed, exposing credentials and data.
controls.recommendation: Remove the rsh client.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge rsh-client'.

controls.title: Ensure talk client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the talk client (talk) is not installed.
controls.rationale: talk is an unauthenticated, clear-text chat tool with no business use on servers.
controls.business_impact: It adds legacy network code that serves no purpose on a managed server.
controls.recommendation: Remove the talk client.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge talk'.

controls.title: Ensure telnet client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the Telnet client (telnet, inetutils-telnet, telnet-ssl) is not installed.
controls.rationale: Telnet sessions are unencrypted.
controls.business_impact: Users who connect with Telnet expose their credentials on the network.
controls.recommendation: Remove the Telnet client.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge telnet inetutils-telnet telnet-ssl'.

controls.title: Ensure ldap client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the LDAP client utilities (ldap-utils) is not installed.
controls.rationale: LDAP command-line tools are rarely needed on servers.
controls.business_impact: Directory query tools make reconnaissance of the directory easier for an attacker already on the host.
controls.recommendation: Remove the LDAP client utilities.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge ldap-utils'.

controls.title: Ensure ftp client is not installed
controls.description: Checks that the FTP/TFTP client (ftp, tnftp, atftp, inetutils-ftp, ftp-ssl) is not installed.
controls.rationale: FTP clients transfer credentials and data without encryption.
controls.business_impact: FTP use exposes credentials and data to network interception.
controls.recommendation: Remove the FTP/TFTP client.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge ftp tnftp atftp inetutils-ftp ftp-ssl'.

controls.title: Ensure a single time synchronization daemon is in use
controls.description: Checks that exactly one of systemd-timesyncd and chrony is enabled or running.
controls.rationale: Accurate, consistent time is required for log correlation, authentication protocols and certificate validation.
controls.business_impact: No time source makes logs unreliable in an investigation; two competing daemons cause clock instability.
controls.recommendation: Run exactly one time synchronization daemon.
controls.remediation: Enable one daemon ('systemctl enable --now systemd-timesyncd' or install chrony) and disable or remove the other.

controls.title: Ensure systemd-timesyncd configured with authorized timeserver
controls.description: Checks that systemd-timesyncd has NTP or FallbackNTP servers configured (and, if approved_time_servers is set, that only approved servers are used).
controls.rationale: Time should come from authoritative, site-approved sources.
controls.business_impact: Unapproved or default time sources can be spoofed or unavailable, skewing logs and breaking time-dependent security controls.
controls.recommendation: Configure systemd-timesyncd with the approved time servers.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf.d/60-cis.conf with '[Time]', 'NTP=<approved servers>' and 'FallbackNTP=<approved servers>', then 'systemctl restart systemd-timesyncd'.

controls.title: Ensure systemd-timesyncd is enabled and running
controls.description: Checks that systemd-timesyncd.service is enabled and running.
controls.rationale: The configured time source only helps if the daemon runs.
controls.business_impact: A stopped time daemon lets the clock drift, undermining logs and time-based authentication.
controls.recommendation: Enable and start systemd-timesyncd.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask systemd-timesyncd.service' and 'systemctl --now enable systemd-timesyncd.service'.

controls.title: Ensure chrony is configured
controls.description: Checks that chrony has at least one server or pool directive in chrony.conf or its included source files.
controls.rationale: chrony needs an authoritative source to synchronize against.
controls.business_impact: Without a configured source the clock drifts, undermining logs and time-dependent controls.
controls.recommendation: Configure chrony with the approved time servers.
controls.remediation: Add 'server <approved-host> iburst' or 'pool <approved-pool> iburst' lines to /etc/chrony/sources.d/60-cis.sources and run 'chronyc reload sources'.

controls.title: Ensure chrony is running as user _chrony
controls.description: Checks that every running chronyd process runs as the unprivileged _chrony user.
controls.rationale: chronyd processes network input and should run with minimal privileges.
controls.business_impact: A chronyd running as root turns any parsing flaw in its network code into full system compromise.
controls.recommendation: Run chronyd as _chrony.
controls.remediation: Ensure /etc/chrony/chrony.conf does not override 'user _chrony' and that /etc/default/chrony does not pass -u root, then restart chrony.

controls.title: Ensure chrony is enabled and running
controls.description: Checks that chrony.service is enabled and running.
controls.rationale: The configured time source only helps if the daemon runs.
controls.business_impact: A stopped time daemon lets the clock drift, undermining logs and time-based authentication.
controls.recommendation: Enable and start chrony.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask chrony.service' and 'systemctl --now enable chrony.service'.

controls.title: Ensure cron daemon is enabled and active
controls.description: Checks that the cron daemon is enabled and active when cron is installed.
controls.rationale: Scheduled maintenance and security jobs depend on cron running.
controls.business_impact: If cron is stopped, scheduled integrity checks, log rotation and updates silently stop.
controls.recommendation: Enable and start cron.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask cron' and 'systemctl --now enable cron'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/crontab is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron file /etc/crontab is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/crontab defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/crontab learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/crontab to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/crontab' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/crontab'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.hourly is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.hourly is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.hourly defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.hourly learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.hourly to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.hourly' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.hourly'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.daily is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.daily is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.daily defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.daily learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.daily to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.daily' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.daily'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.weekly is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.weekly is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.weekly defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.weekly learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.weekly to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.weekly' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.weekly'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.monthly is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.monthly is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.monthly defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.monthly learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.monthly to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.monthly' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.monthly'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.yearly is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.yearly is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.yearly defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.yearly learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.yearly to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.yearly' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.yearly'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/cron.d is configured
controls.description: Checks that the cron directory /etc/cron.d is owned by root:root and grants no access to group or other.
controls.rationale: /etc/cron.d defines jobs that run as root.
controls.business_impact: A user who can read /etc/cron.d learns scheduled privileged activity; one who can write it can run commands as root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/cron.d to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/cron.d' and 'chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.d'.

controls.title: Ensure access to crontab is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/cron.allow exists and, like any /etc/cron.deny, is owned by root, group root or crontab, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: An allow list limits crontab use to named accounts.
controls.business_impact: Without an allow list any account, including compromised service accounts, can schedule persistent jobs.
controls.recommendation: Create a restrictive /etc/cron.allow listing only approved users.
controls.remediation: Run 'touch /etc/cron.allow', 'chown root:crontab /etc/cron.allow' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/cron.allow'; apply the same ownership and mode to /etc/cron.deny if it exists.

controls.title: Ensure access to at is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/at.allow exists and, like any /etc/at.deny, is owned by root, group root or daemon, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: An allow list limits use of at to named accounts.
controls.business_impact: Without an allow list any account can schedule jobs with at to maintain persistence.
controls.recommendation: Create a restrictive /etc/at.allow listing only approved users.
controls.remediation: Run 'touch /etc/at.allow', 'chown root:daemon /etc/at.allow' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/at.allow'; apply the same to /etc/at.deny if it exists.

controls.title: Ensure wireless interfaces are not available
controls.description: Checks that the driver module of any wireless interface is not loaded, not loadable and deny-listed.
controls.rationale: Servers should not have active wireless interfaces.
controls.business_impact: An active wireless interface can bridge the server to an uncontrolled network, bypassing firewalls and monitoring.
controls.recommendation: Disable wireless interfaces on servers.
controls.remediation: Run 'nmcli radio all off' if NetworkManager is used, then add 'install <driver> /bin/false' and 'blacklist <driver>' for each wireless driver in /etc/modprobe.d/.

controls.title: Ensure bluetooth services are not in use
controls.description: Checks that the Bluetooth stack (bluez) is not installed or, when required as a dependency, that bluetooth.service is neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: Servers rarely have a legitimate need for Bluetooth.
controls.business_impact: Bluetooth exposes the host to nearby attackers and has a history of remotely exploitable flaws.
controls.recommendation: Remove or disable Bluetooth.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt purge bluez'; if it is a required dependency run 'systemctl --now mask bluetooth.service'.

controls.title: Ensure atm kernel module is not available
controls.description: Checks that the atm kernel module (the Asynchronous Transfer Mode networking) cannot be used: it is either absent, or unloaded, deny-listed and mapped to a disabled install command.
controls.rationale: Kernel code that the system never needs still enlarges its attack surface; making the module unloadable removes it as an attack path.
controls.business_impact: Unprivileged users can make the kernel load the atm protocol by opening a socket, exposing rarely used code that has contained privilege-escalation and remote vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Disable the atm module unless a documented business need requires it.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/modprobe.d/atm.conf containing 'install atm /bin/false' and 'blacklist atm', then unload it with 'modprobe -r atm'.

controls.title: Ensure can kernel module is not available
controls.description: Checks that the can kernel module (the Controller Area Network protocol) cannot be used: it is either absent, or unloaded, deny-listed and mapped to a disabled install command.
controls.rationale: Kernel code that the system never needs still enlarges its attack surface; making the module unloadable removes it as an attack path.
controls.business_impact: Unprivileged users can make the kernel load the can protocol by opening a socket, exposing rarely used code that has contained privilege-escalation and remote vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Disable the can module unless a documented business need requires it.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/modprobe.d/can.conf containing 'install can /bin/false' and 'blacklist can', then unload it with 'modprobe -r can'.

controls.title: Ensure dccp kernel module is not available
controls.description: Checks that the dccp kernel module (the Datagram Congestion Control Protocol) cannot be used: it is either absent, or unloaded, deny-listed and mapped to a disabled install command.
controls.rationale: Kernel code that the system never needs still enlarges its attack surface; making the module unloadable removes it as an attack path.
controls.business_impact: Unprivileged users can make the kernel load the dccp protocol by opening a socket, exposing rarely used code that has contained privilege-escalation and remote vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Disable the dccp module unless a documented business need requires it.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/modprobe.d/dccp.conf containing 'install dccp /bin/false' and 'blacklist dccp', then unload it with 'modprobe -r dccp'.

controls.title: Ensure rds kernel module is not available
controls.description: Checks that the rds kernel module (the Reliable Datagram Sockets protocol) cannot be used: it is either absent, or unloaded, deny-listed and mapped to a disabled install command.
controls.rationale: Kernel code that the system never needs still enlarges its attack surface; making the module unloadable removes it as an attack path.
controls.business_impact: Unprivileged users can make the kernel load the rds protocol by opening a socket, exposing rarely used code that has contained privilege-escalation and remote vulnerabilities.
controls.recommendation: Disable the rds module unless a documented business need requires it.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/modprobe.d/rds.conf containing 'install rds /bin/false' and 'blacklist rds', then unload it with 'modprobe -r rds'.

controls.title: Ensure net.ipv4.ip_forward is configured
controls.description: Checks that net.ipv4.ip_forward is 0 both in the running kernel and in the sysctl configuration applied at boot.
controls.rationale: A host that is not a router must not forward packets between interfaces.
controls.business_impact: IP forwarding lets the host route traffic between networks, bypassing network segmentation.
controls.recommendation: Set net.ipv4.ip_forward to 0 persistently.
controls.remediation: Add 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0' to /etc/sysctl.d/60-cis.conf, remove or correct conflicting entries in other sysctl files, then run 'sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0' and 'sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1'.

notes.proxmox: Forwarding is needed only when the node routes or masquerades guest traffic (routed or NAT setups, SDN); nodes that only bridge guests through vmbr interfaces do not need it.

controls.title: Ensure ufw is installed
controls.description: Checks that Uncomplicated Firewall (ufw) is installed.
controls.rationale: A host firewall limits which services are reachable, independent of network firewalls.
controls.business_impact: Without a host firewall every listening service is exposed to any host that can route to the server.
controls.recommendation: Install ufw (or document the equivalent host firewall in use).
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install ufw'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE provides its own firewall (pve-firewall) and UFW conflicts with it, so do not install UFW on a node. Enforce host filtering with the Proxmox VE firewall instead: enable it at datacenter and node level with a default-deny input policy ('pve-firewall status' shows whether it is running).

controls.title: Ensure ufw service is configured
controls.description: Checks that ufw.service is enabled and active and that 'ufw status' reports Status: active.
controls.rationale: The firewall only protects the host while its rules are loaded.
controls.business_impact: An installed but inactive firewall leaves every listening service exposed.
controls.recommendation: Enable UFW and its service.
controls.remediation: Allow required inbound services first (for example 'ufw allow proto tcp from <admin-net> to any port 22'), then run 'ufw enable' and 'systemctl --now enable ufw'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE provides its own firewall (pve-firewall) and UFW conflicts with it, so do not install UFW on a node. Enforce host filtering with the Proxmox VE firewall instead: enable it at datacenter and node level with a default-deny input policy ('pve-firewall status' shows whether it is running).

controls.title: Ensure ufw incoming default is configured
controls.description: Checks that UFW is active and its default incoming policy is deny or reject.
controls.rationale: Inbound traffic should be denied unless a rule explicitly allows it.
controls.business_impact: A permissive default incoming policy allows any traffic that no rule explicitly blocks.
controls.recommendation: Set the UFW default incoming policy to deny.
controls.remediation: Create allow rules for required traffic, then run 'ufw default deny incoming'.

controls.description: Checks that UFW is active and its default outgoing policy is deny or reject.
controls.rationale: Outbound traffic should be limited to approved destinations to hinder data exfiltration and command-and-control.
controls.business_impact: A permissive default outgoing policy allows any traffic that no rule explicitly blocks.
controls.recommendation: Set the UFW default outgoing policy to deny.
controls.remediation: Create allow rules for required traffic, then run 'ufw default deny outgoing'.

controls.rationale: Traffic routed through the host should be denied by default.
controls.business_impact: A permissive default routed policy allows any traffic that no rule explicitly blocks.
controls.recommendation: Set the UFW default routed policy to deny.
controls.remediation: Create allow rules for required traffic, then run 'ufw default deny routed'.
