controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/ssh/sshd_config is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/ssh/sshd_config is root:root with mode 0600 or stricter and that included .conf drop-ins are root:root with no group or other access.
controls.rationale: The SSH daemon configuration controls how every remote login is authenticated.
controls.business_impact: A user who can change the sshd configuration can enable weak authentication or root login; readable files reveal the access policy.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the sshd configuration files to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf' and 'chmod u-x,og-rwx' on each file.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ directory is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d and any other Include directory are root:root with no group or other access.
controls.rationale: Drop-in directories can add or override sshd settings.
controls.business_impact: A writable drop-in directory lets an unprivileged user add an sshd configuration that weakens authentication.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the sshd drop-in directories to root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d' and 'chmod 0700 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d'.

controls.title: Ensure access to SSH private host key files is configured
controls.description: Checks that every private SSH host key used by sshd is root:root with mode 0600.
controls.rationale: Host private keys prove the server's identity to clients.
controls.business_impact: A stolen host key lets an attacker impersonate the server and intercept SSH sessions and credentials.
controls.recommendation: Restrict private host keys to root with mode 0600.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key' and 'chmod 0600 /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key'.

controls.title: Ensure access to SSH public host key files is configured
controls.description: Checks that every public SSH host key is root:root and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: Public host keys must not be replaceable by other users.
controls.business_impact: A modified public host key can confuse key verification and host-based trust.
controls.recommendation: Restrict public host keys to root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub' and 'chmod u-x,go-wx /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd access is configured
controls.description: Checks that sshd restricts logins with AllowUsers, AllowGroups, DenyUsers or DenyGroups.
controls.rationale: Explicit access lists limit SSH logins to accounts with a business need.
controls.business_impact: Without an access list every local account with a password or key, including service accounts, can attempt SSH logins.
controls.recommendation: Restrict SSH logins to approved users or groups.
controls.remediation: Add for example 'AllowGroups ssh-users' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Match block, then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

notes.proxmox: On Proxmox VE cluster nodes AllowUsers/AllowGroups must still admit root from the other cluster nodes, or migration and replication fail.

controls.title: Ensure sshd Banner is configured
controls.description: Checks that sshd presents a Banner file and that the banner does not disclose the operating system.
controls.rationale: A pre-authentication banner states the terms of authorized use.
controls.business_impact: Without a banner the organization weakens its legal position against unauthorized access; a revealing banner aids fingerprinting.
controls.recommendation: Configure an approved SSH banner.
controls.remediation: Add 'Banner /etc/issue.net' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf, place an approved notice in that file, then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd Ciphers are configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that no CBC, arcfour or other weak cipher is offered.
controls.rationale: Weak and CBC-mode ciphers have known cryptographic weaknesses.
controls.business_impact: Weak ciphers can allow recovery of plaintext from captured SSH sessions.
controls.recommendation: Set Ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'Ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

check.informational: If chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com is offered, confirm OpenSSH includes the CVE-2023-48795 (Terrapin) strict key exchange fix; Debian 13 does.

controls.title: Ensure sshd ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are both greater than zero.
controls.rationale: Keep-alive probes let sshd detect and close dead or abandoned sessions.
controls.business_impact: Abandoned sessions stay open indefinitely and can be hijacked or reused.
controls.recommendation: Set ClientAliveInterval 15 and ClientAliveCountMax 3 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'ClientAliveInterval 15 and ClientAliveCountMax 3' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd DisableForwarding is enabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that DisableForwarding is yes.
controls.rationale: Port, agent, X11 and stream-local forwarding can tunnel traffic through the server.
controls.business_impact: SSH forwarding can bypass network controls and expose internal services to remote users.
controls.recommendation: Set DisableForwarding yes in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'DisableForwarding yes' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE secure (default) live migration tunnels guest state through SSH socket forwarding between cluster nodes; DisableForwarding yes breaks it unless forwarding is re-allowed for root from cluster node addresses in a Match block.

controls.title: Ensure sshd GSSAPIAuthentication is disabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that GSSAPIAuthentication is no.
controls.rationale: GSSAPI authentication adds complexity and attack surface when Kerberos is not used.
controls.business_impact: Unneeded authentication methods increase the code reachable before authentication.
controls.recommendation: Set GSSAPIAuthentication no in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'GSSAPIAuthentication no' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd HostbasedAuthentication is disabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that HostbasedAuthentication is no.
controls.rationale: Host-based authentication trusts other hosts instead of verifying users.
controls.business_impact: A compromise of any trusted host grants SSH access to this server without user credentials.
controls.recommendation: Set HostbasedAuthentication no in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'HostbasedAuthentication no' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd IgnoreRhosts is enabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that IgnoreRhosts is yes.
controls.rationale: .rhosts and .shosts files grant access based on host names.
controls.business_impact: Legacy trust files could let users grant password-less access from arbitrary hosts.
controls.recommendation: Set IgnoreRhosts yes in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'IgnoreRhosts yes' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd KexAlgorithms is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that no SHA-1 based Diffie-Hellman key exchange is offered.
controls.rationale: SHA-1 based key exchange algorithms are cryptographically weak.
controls.business_impact: Weak key exchange lowers the cost of attacking captured sessions and invites downgrade attacks.
controls.recommendation: Set KexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'KexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd LoginGraceTime is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that LoginGraceTime is between 1 and 60 seconds.
controls.rationale: A short login grace period limits unauthenticated connections held open.
controls.business_impact: Long grace periods let attackers tie up connection slots and slow brute-force detection.
controls.recommendation: Set LoginGraceTime 60 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'LoginGraceTime 60' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd LogLevel is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that LogLevel is VERBOSE or INFO.
controls.rationale: SSH logins, including key fingerprints, must be logged for accountability.
controls.business_impact: Too little SSH logging leaves unauthorized access undetected and hampers investigations.
controls.recommendation: Set LogLevel VERBOSE in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'LogLevel VERBOSE' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd MACs are configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that no MD5, RIPEMD-160, truncated SHA-1 or 64-bit UMAC message authentication code is offered.
controls.rationale: Weak MACs undermine the integrity protection of SSH traffic.
controls.business_impact: Weak integrity protection makes tampering with SSH sessions more feasible.
controls.recommendation: Set MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd MaxAuthTries is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that MaxAuthTries is 4 or less.
controls.rationale: Limiting authentication attempts per connection slows password guessing.
controls.business_impact: Many attempts per connection make brute-force attacks faster and quieter.
controls.recommendation: Set MaxAuthTries 4 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'MaxAuthTries 4' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd MaxSessions is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that MaxSessions is 10 or less and no configuration file (including Match blocks) sets it higher.
controls.rationale: Limiting sessions per connection bounds resource use.
controls.business_impact: Unlimited multiplexed sessions allow resource exhaustion from a single connection.
controls.recommendation: Set MaxSessions 10 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'MaxSessions 10' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd MaxStartups is configured
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that MaxStartups is 10:30:60 or more restrictive.
controls.rationale: MaxStartups throttles concurrent unauthenticated connections.
controls.business_impact: Without throttling an attacker can exhaust connection slots and deny legitimate administrative access.
controls.recommendation: Set MaxStartups 10:30:60 in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'MaxStartups 10:30:60' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that PermitEmptyPasswords is no.
controls.rationale: Accounts with empty passwords must never be reachable over SSH.
controls.business_impact: Any account with an empty password could be logged into remotely without credentials.
controls.recommendation: Set PermitEmptyPasswords no in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'PermitEmptyPasswords no' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that PermitRootLogin is no.
controls.rationale: Administrators should log in with named accounts and escalate with sudo.
controls.business_impact: Direct root login removes accountability and makes root the single target of password and key attacks.
controls.recommendation: Set PermitRootLogin no in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'PermitRootLogin no' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

notes.proxmox: Proxmox VE cluster nodes use key-based root SSH between members (migration, replication, joining nodes). The usual compromise is 'PermitRootLogin prohibit-password' with root access limited to the cluster network through a Match Address block.

controls.title: Ensure sshd PermitUserEnvironment is disabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that PermitUserEnvironment is no.
controls.rationale: User-supplied environment variables can alter program behaviour at login.
controls.business_impact: Users could set variables such as LD_PRELOAD to bypass restrictions on their SSH sessions.
controls.recommendation: Set PermitUserEnvironment no in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'PermitUserEnvironment no' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sshd UsePAM is enabled
controls.description: Checks the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T in the root/local-host context CIS uses) to confirm that UsePAM is yes.
controls.rationale: PAM enforces account, password and session policy for SSH logins.
controls.business_impact: Without PAM, lockout, password quality and session controls do not apply to SSH.
controls.recommendation: Set UsePAM yes in the sshd configuration.
controls.remediation: Add 'UsePAM yes' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf above any Include or Match entries (sshd uses the first value it reads), then run 'systemctl reload ssh'.

controls.title: Ensure sudo is installed
controls.description: Checks that sudo or sudo-rs is installed (or libsss-sudo with sssd when sudoers come from a directory).
controls.rationale: sudo provides accountable, least-privilege administration instead of shared root logins.
controls.business_impact: Without sudo, administrators share the root password and actions cannot be attributed to individuals.
controls.recommendation: Install sudo or sudo-rs.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install sudo' (or 'apt install sudo-rs').

controls.title: Ensure sudo commands use pty
controls.description: Checks that sudoers explicitly sets 'Defaults use_pty' and never negates it.
controls.rationale: Running commands in a pseudo-terminal stops them from injecting input into the invoking terminal after sudo exits.
controls.business_impact: Without use_pty a malicious command run with sudo can keep running and push keystrokes into the administrator's terminal.
controls.recommendation: Set Defaults use_pty.
controls.remediation: Run 'visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/60-cis' and add 'Defaults use_pty'; remove any '!use_pty'.

controls.title: Ensure sudo log file exists
controls.description: Checks that sudo activity is logged, either to a dedicated logfile (classic sudo) or to the journal/auth.log.
controls.rationale: A record of privileged commands supports accountability and investigation.
controls.business_impact: Without a sudo log, privileged actions cannot be reconstructed after an incident.
controls.recommendation: Ensure sudo usage is logged.
controls.remediation: For classic sudo run 'visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/60-cis' and add 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo.log"'; for sudo-rs confirm sudo events reach journald or rsyslog.

controls.title: Ensure users must provide password for escalation
controls.description: Checks that no sudoers rule uses the NOPASSWD tag.
controls.rationale: Re-entering a password before privilege escalation confirms the user is present.
controls.business_impact: With NOPASSWD, anyone who gains a user's session, even without the password, obtains that user's sudo privileges.
controls.recommendation: Remove NOPASSWD from sudoers rules.
controls.remediation: Edit the reported files with 'visudo' and remove the NOPASSWD tags (automation accounts should use tightly scoped, documented exceptions).

controls.title: Ensure re-authentication for privilege escalation is not disabled globally
controls.description: Checks that no sudoers entry disables authentication with !authenticate.
controls.rationale: sudo must re-authenticate users before granting privileges.
controls.business_impact: Disabling authentication turns any compromised user session into immediate root access.
controls.recommendation: Remove !authenticate from sudoers.
controls.remediation: Edit the reported files with 'visudo' and remove every '!authenticate' entry.

controls.title: Ensure sudo timestamp_timeout is configured
controls.description: Checks that sudo's timestamp_timeout is explicitly set to between 0 and 15 minutes.
controls.rationale: A bounded credential cache limits how long sudo stays unlocked after authentication.
controls.business_impact: A long or unlimited timeout lets anyone at an unattended terminal run privileged commands.
controls.recommendation: Set timestamp_timeout to 15 minutes or less.
controls.remediation: Run 'visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/60-cis' and add 'Defaults timestamp_timeout=15'.

controls.title: Ensure access to the su command is restricted
controls.description: Checks that /etc/pam.d/su requires pam_wheel.so with use_uid and a group= argument naming an empty group.
controls.rationale: Restricting su forces administrators to use sudo, which is logged and scoped.
controls.business_impact: Unrestricted su lets any user who learns the root password become root without an audit trail.
controls.recommendation: Restrict su to an empty, dedicated group.
controls.remediation: Run 'groupadd sugroup' and add 'auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=sugroup' to /etc/pam.d/su.

controls.title: Ensure latest version of pam is installed
controls.description: Checks that libpam-runtime is installed and that APT knows of no newer version.
controls.rationale: Authentication modules must include the latest security fixes.
controls.business_impact: An outdated libpam-runtime can leave known authentication vulnerabilities unpatched.
controls.recommendation: Install the latest libpam-runtime.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt update' and 'apt install libpam-runtime' (or 'apt upgrade').

controls.title: Ensure latest version of libpam-modules is installed
controls.description: Checks that libpam-modules is installed and that APT knows of no newer version.
controls.rationale: Authentication modules must include the latest security fixes.
controls.business_impact: An outdated libpam-modules can leave known authentication vulnerabilities unpatched.
controls.recommendation: Install the latest libpam-modules.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt update' and 'apt install libpam-modules' (or 'apt upgrade').

controls.title: Ensure latest version of libpam-pwquality is installed
controls.description: Checks that libpam-pwquality is installed and that APT knows of no newer version.
controls.rationale: Authentication modules must include the latest security fixes.
controls.business_impact: An outdated libpam-pwquality can leave known authentication vulnerabilities unpatched.
controls.recommendation: Install the latest libpam-pwquality.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt update' and 'apt install libpam-pwquality' (or 'apt upgrade').

controls.title: Ensure latest version of cracklib-runtime is installed
controls.description: Checks that cracklib-runtime is installed and that APT knows of no newer version.
controls.rationale: Authentication modules must include the latest security fixes.
controls.business_impact: An outdated cracklib-runtime can leave known authentication vulnerabilities unpatched.
controls.recommendation: Install the latest cracklib-runtime.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt update' and 'apt install cracklib-runtime' (or 'apt upgrade').

controls.title: Ensure pam_unix module is enabled
controls.description: Checks that pam_unix.so is present in the required Debian common PAM stacks.
controls.rationale: pam_unix provides standard password authentication and account checks.
controls.business_impact: If pam_unix is missing from a stack, local password, expiry or session controls may silently stop applying.
controls.recommendation: Enable pam_unix.so in the common PAM configuration.
controls.remediation: Run 'pam-auth-update --enable unix'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_faillock module is enabled
controls.description: Checks that pam_faillock.so is present in the required Debian common PAM stacks.
controls.rationale: pam_faillock locks accounts after repeated failed authentication attempts.
controls.business_impact: Without account lockout, online password guessing against local accounts is unlimited.
controls.recommendation: Enable pam_faillock.so in the common PAM configuration.
controls.remediation: Create pam-auth-update profiles for faillock and faillock_notify under /usr/share/pam-configs (preauth, authfail and account entries) and run 'pam-auth-update --enable faillock --enable faillock_notify'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_pwquality module is enabled
controls.description: Checks that pam_pwquality.so is present in the required Debian common PAM stacks.
controls.rationale: pam_pwquality enforces password strength when passwords are changed.
controls.business_impact: Without it users can choose trivially guessable passwords.
controls.recommendation: Enable pam_pwquality.so in the common PAM configuration.
controls.remediation: Install libpam-pwquality and run 'pam-auth-update --enable pwquality'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_pwhistory module is enabled
controls.description: Checks that pam_pwhistory.so is present in the required Debian common PAM stacks.
controls.rationale: pam_pwhistory prevents reuse of recent passwords.
controls.business_impact: Without history enforcement users can cycle back to compromised passwords.
controls.recommendation: Enable pam_pwhistory.so in the common PAM configuration.
controls.remediation: Create a pwhistory profile in /usr/share/pam-configs (password requisite pam_pwhistory.so use_authtok) and run 'pam-auth-update --enable pwhistory'.

controls.title: Ensure password failed attempts lockout is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/security/faillock.conf sets deny to 5 or fewer failures and that no pam_faillock.so argument overrides it with 0 or more than 5.
controls.rationale: Locking accounts after a few failures stops online password guessing.
controls.business_impact: A high or disabled failure limit lets attackers keep guessing passwords.
controls.recommendation: Lock accounts after at most 5 failed attempts.
controls.remediation: Set 'deny = 5' in /etc/security/faillock.conf and remove deny= arguments from pam_faillock.so lines in /etc/pam.d/common-auth.

controls.title: Ensure password unlock time is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/security/faillock.conf sets unlock_time to 0 (manual unlock) or at least 900 seconds and that no pam_faillock.so argument overrides it with a shorter time.
controls.rationale: A lockout period long enough to deter guessing makes lockout effective.
controls.business_impact: A short unlock time lets automated guessing resume almost immediately.
controls.recommendation: Set unlock_time to 900 seconds or more (or 0).
controls.remediation: Set 'unlock_time = 900' in /etc/security/faillock.conf and remove unlock_time= arguments shorter than 900 from /etc/pam.d/common-auth.

controls.title: Ensure password failed attempts lockout includes root account
controls.description: Checks that faillock.conf sets even_deny_root and/or root_unlock_time, and that any root_unlock_time is at least 60 seconds.
controls.rationale: The root account is the most valuable target for password guessing.
controls.business_impact: If root is exempt from lockout, its password can be guessed without limit wherever root can authenticate.
controls.recommendation: Apply failed-login lockout to root.
controls.remediation: Add 'even_deny_root' and 'root_unlock_time = 60' to /etc/security/faillock.conf.

controls.title: Ensure password number of changed characters is configured
controls.description: Checks that difok is set to 2 or more, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: New passwords should differ meaningfully from the previous one.
controls.business_impact: Users can make trivial changes to an old, possibly compromised password.
controls.recommendation: Configure difok = 2 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'difok = 2' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting difok values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password length is configured
controls.description: Checks that the minimum password length is 14 or more, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Password length is the strongest single factor in resistance to guessing and cracking.
controls.business_impact: Short passwords can be cracked quickly from captured hashes or guessed online.
controls.recommendation: Configure minlen = 14 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'minlen = 14' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting minlen values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password same consecutive characters is configured
controls.description: Checks that maxrepeat is between 1 and 3, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Limiting repeated characters removes an easy way to reach the length requirement.
controls.business_impact: Passwords such as 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaa' satisfy length but are trivially guessed.
controls.recommendation: Configure maxrepeat = 3 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'maxrepeat = 3' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting maxrepeat values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password maximum sequential characters is configured
controls.description: Checks that maxsequence is between 1 and 3, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Limiting monotonic sequences removes predictable patterns.
controls.business_impact: Passwords such as '12345678901234' satisfy length but are among the first guessed.
controls.recommendation: Configure maxsequence = 3 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'maxsequence = 3' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting maxsequence values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password dictionary check is enabled
controls.description: Checks that the dictionary check is not disabled, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Dictionary words are the first candidates in password guessing.
controls.business_impact: Passwords based on dictionary words are cracked quickly.
controls.recommendation: Configure dictcheck = 1 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'dictcheck = 1' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting dictcheck values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password quality checking is enforced
controls.description: Checks that password quality rules are enforced rather than only warned about, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Quality checks must reject weak passwords, not just warn.
controls.business_impact: In warn-only mode users can still set weak passwords.
controls.recommendation: Configure enforcing = 1 for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'enforcing = 1' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting enforcing values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password quality is enforced for the root user
controls.description: Checks that password quality rules also apply when root sets passwords, honouring pwquality precedence (module arguments, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d).
controls.rationale: Administrators setting passwords should meet the same quality bar.
controls.business_impact: Weak passwords set by root for users or itself bypass the policy.
controls.recommendation: Configure enforce_for_root for pam_pwquality.
controls.remediation: Add 'enforce_for_root' to /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf and remove conflicting enforce_for_root values from pwquality.conf and the pam_pwquality.so arguments in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password history remember is configured
controls.description: Checks that the last 24 or more passwords are remembered, configured in exactly one place (pwhistory.conf or the pam_pwhistory.so arguments).
controls.rationale: Password history stops users from cycling back to old passwords.
controls.business_impact: Users can return to a password that was previously exposed.
controls.recommendation: Configure remember = 24 for pam_pwhistory.
controls.remediation: Set 'remember = 24' in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf (or on the pam_pwhistory.so line, but not both) and keep pam_pwhistory.so enabled in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure password history is enforced for the root user
controls.description: Checks that password history is also enforced for root, configured in exactly one place (pwhistory.conf or the pam_pwhistory.so arguments).
controls.rationale: Root should follow the same reuse rules.
controls.business_impact: Root could reuse an exposed password.
controls.recommendation: Configure enforce_for_root for pam_pwhistory.
controls.remediation: Set 'enforce_for_root' in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf (or on the pam_pwhistory.so line, but not both) and keep pam_pwhistory.so enabled in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure pam_pwhistory includes use_authtok
controls.description: Checks that pam_pwhistory uses the password already accepted by earlier modules (use_authtok), configured in exactly one place (pwhistory.conf or the pam_pwhistory.so arguments).
controls.rationale: Using the token from the stack ensures every module checks the same password.
controls.business_impact: Without use_authtok the history check may prompt separately or evaluate a different value.
controls.recommendation: Configure use_authtok for pam_pwhistory.
controls.remediation: Set 'use_authtok' in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf (or on the pam_pwhistory.so line, but not both) and keep pam_pwhistory.so enabled in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

controls.title: Ensure pam_unix does not include nullok
controls.description: Checks that pam_unix.so is not given the nullok argument in any common PAM stack.
controls.rationale: nullok allows authentication to accounts with empty passwords.
controls.business_impact: Any account with an empty password field could be logged into without credentials.
controls.recommendation: Remove nullok from pam_unix.so.
controls.remediation: Remove 'nullok' from the pam_unix.so lines in /usr/share/pam-configs/unix (or /etc/pam.d/common-*) and run 'pam-auth-update --enable unix'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_unix does not include remember
controls.description: Checks that pam_unix.so is not given the remember= argument.
controls.rationale: Password history belongs in pam_pwhistory, which stores it more securely than pam_unix.
controls.business_impact: pam_unix history uses the legacy /etc/security/opasswd handling and duplicates policy in a weaker place.
controls.recommendation: Remove remember= from pam_unix.so and use pam_pwhistory.
controls.remediation: Remove 'remember=<N>' from the pam_unix.so lines in /usr/share/pam-configs/unix and run 'pam-auth-update --enable unix'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_unix includes a strong password hashing algorithm
controls.description: Checks that every pam_unix.so password entry specifies sha512 or yescrypt.
controls.rationale: Strong, slow password hashing resists offline cracking.
controls.business_impact: Weak hashes allow stolen password databases to be cracked quickly.
controls.recommendation: Use yescrypt (or sha512) for pam_unix password hashing.
controls.remediation: Add 'yescrypt' to the pam_unix.so password line in /usr/share/pam-configs/unix and run 'pam-auth-update --enable unix'.

controls.title: Ensure pam_unix includes use_authtok
controls.description: Checks that every pam_unix.so password entry includes use_authtok.
controls.rationale: use_authtok makes pam_unix set the password that earlier modules (such as pwquality) already approved.
controls.business_impact: Without it the quality checks could be bypassed by a separate prompt.
controls.recommendation: Add use_authtok to pam_unix.so password entries.
controls.remediation: Add 'use_authtok' to the pam_unix.so password line in /usr/share/pam-configs/unix and run 'pam-auth-update --enable unix'.

controls.title: Ensure password expiration is configured
controls.description: Checks that PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs and the maximum age of every account with a password are between 1 and 365 days.
controls.rationale: Periodic password expiry limits how long a compromised password remains useful.
controls.business_impact: Passwords that never expire give an attacker indefinite access after a single compromise.
controls.recommendation: Set a maximum password age of 365 days or less.
controls.remediation: Set 'PASS_MAX_DAYS 365' in /etc/login.defs and run 'chage --maxdays 365 <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure password expiration warning days is configured
controls.description: Checks that PASS_WARN_AGE and each account's password expiry warning are 7 days or more.
controls.rationale: Advance warning lets users change passwords before they expire.
controls.business_impact: Users surprised by expiry tend to choose weak replacement passwords or get locked out.
controls.recommendation: Warn users at least 7 days before password expiry.
controls.remediation: Set 'PASS_WARN_AGE 7' in /etc/login.defs and run 'chage --warndays 7 <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure strong password hashing algorithm is configured
controls.description: Checks that ENCRYPT_METHOD in /etc/login.defs is SHA512 or YESCRYPT.
controls.rationale: The shadow tools use this algorithm when they set passwords.
controls.business_impact: A weak algorithm lets stolen password hashes be cracked quickly.
controls.recommendation: Use YESCRYPT (or SHA512) for password hashing.
controls.remediation: Set 'ENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT' in /etc/login.defs.

controls.title: Ensure inactive password lock is configured
controls.description: Checks that the useradd default INACTIVE and the inactivity period of every account with a password are between 0 and 45 days.
controls.rationale: Accounts whose passwords have expired should be disabled after a short grace period.
controls.business_impact: Dormant accounts with expired passwords remain a target that nobody is watching.
controls.recommendation: Lock accounts 45 days or less after password expiry.
controls.remediation: Run 'useradd -D -f 45' and 'chage --inactive 45 <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
controls.description: Checks that no account with a password has a last-change date in the future.
controls.rationale: A future change date breaks password ageing for that account.
controls.business_impact: Accounts with future change dates never reach expiry, defeating password ageing.
controls.recommendation: Correct future password change dates.
controls.remediation: Investigate the reported accounts and reset the date with 'chage --lastday <YYYY-MM-DD> <user>' or force a password change.

controls.title: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
controls.description: Checks that root is the only account with UID 0.
controls.rationale: Any UID 0 account has full root privileges.
controls.business_impact: An extra UID 0 account is a hidden root backdoor that bypasses controls aimed at root.
controls.recommendation: Remove or renumber any non-root UID 0 account.
controls.remediation: Investigate each reported account, then delete it or assign a new UID with 'usermod -u <uid> <user>'.

controls.title: Ensure root is the only GID 0 account
controls.description: Checks that root is the only account whose primary group is GID 0 (sync, shutdown, halt and operator are excluded, as in CIS).
controls.rationale: Membership of the root group grants access to root-group-owned files.
controls.business_impact: Accounts in GID 0 can read or modify sensitive root-group files.
controls.recommendation: Assign non-root accounts a different primary group.
controls.remediation: Run 'usermod -g <group> <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure group root is the only GID 0 group
controls.description: Checks that the root group is the only group with GID 0.
controls.rationale: Another group with GID 0 is effectively the root group under a different name.
controls.business_impact: Members of a duplicate GID 0 group gain root-group access without appearing in the root group.
controls.recommendation: Renumber or remove duplicate GID 0 groups.
controls.remediation: Run 'groupmod -g <gid> <group>' or remove the group after moving its members.

controls.title: Ensure root account access is controlled
controls.description: Checks that the root account either has a password set or is locked (passwd -S status P or L).
controls.rationale: Root access must always require authentication.
controls.business_impact: A root account with no password could be entered without credentials.
controls.recommendation: Set a strong root password or lock the root account.
controls.remediation: Run 'passwd root' to set a strong password, or 'usermod -L root' if root logins are not needed.

controls.title: Ensure root path integrity
controls.description: Checks that root's login PATH has no empty or current-directory entries and that every entry is an existing, root-owned directory without group or other write access.
controls.rationale: Root runs commands by name; every PATH entry must be trustworthy.
controls.business_impact: A writable or relative PATH entry lets an attacker plant a trojan that root executes, leading to full compromise.
controls.recommendation: Make root's PATH contain only secure, root-owned directories.
controls.remediation: Correct PATH in /root/.profile, /root/.bashrc and /etc/profile, and run 'chown root:root' and 'chmod go-w' on each reported directory.

controls.title: Ensure root user umask is configured
controls.description: Checks that /root/.profile and /root/.bashrc do not set a umask less restrictive than 0027.
controls.rationale: root's umask decides the default permissions of files root creates.
controls.business_impact: A permissive root umask creates files that other users can read or modify.
controls.recommendation: Set root's umask to 0027 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Set 'umask 0027' in /root/.profile and /root/.bashrc and remove less restrictive umask lines.

controls.title: Ensure system accounts do not have a valid login shell
controls.description: Checks that system accounts (UID below UID_MIN, or 65534) other than root, halt, sync, shutdown and nfsnobody have no valid login shell.
controls.rationale: Service accounts should never be usable for interactive logins.
controls.business_impact: A service account with a shell can be used for interactive access if its credentials or keys leak.
controls.recommendation: Set a nologin shell on system accounts.
controls.remediation: Run 'usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure accounts without a valid login shell are locked
controls.description: Checks that every non-root account without a valid login shell is locked (passwd -S status L).
controls.rationale: Accounts that are not meant for login should not have usable passwords.
controls.business_impact: An unlocked non-login account could still authenticate to services that do not check the shell.
controls.recommendation: Lock accounts that have no valid login shell.
controls.remediation: Run 'usermod -L <user>' for each reported account.

controls.title: Ensure nologin is not listed in /etc/shells
controls.description: Checks that /etc/shells does not list nologin.
controls.rationale: /etc/shells lists shells that are valid for login; nologin is not one.
controls.business_impact: Listing nologin can let restricted accounts be treated as having a valid shell by FTP and other services.
controls.recommendation: Remove nologin from /etc/shells.
controls.remediation: Delete any '/usr/sbin/nologin' or '/sbin/nologin' line from /etc/shells.

controls.title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
controls.description: Checks that TMOUT is set to 900 seconds or less, readonly and exported in /etc/profile, /etc/profile.d or /etc/bash.bashrc.
controls.rationale: An idle shell timeout closes unattended interactive sessions.
controls.business_impact: Unattended root or user shells can be used by anyone with physical or session access.
controls.recommendation: Configure a readonly, exported TMOUT of 900 seconds or less.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/profile.d/60-cis-tmout.sh containing 'TMOUT=900', 'readonly TMOUT' and 'export TMOUT', and remove other TMOUT settings.

controls.title: Ensure default user umask is configured
controls.description: Checks that every umask in /etc/profile and /etc/profile.d/*.sh, and UMASK in /etc/login.defs, is 027 or more restrictive, and that a system-wide umask is configured.
controls.rationale: The default umask decides whether new files are readable by other users.
controls.business_impact: A permissive default umask exposes users' new files to everyone on the system.
controls.recommendation: Set a system-wide umask of 027 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Set 'UMASK 027' in /etc/login.defs and create /etc/profile.d/60-cis-umask.sh containing 'umask 027'; correct any less restrictive umask lines.

controls.title: Ensure journald service is active
controls.description: Checks that systemd-journald.service is active.
controls.rationale: journald collects kernel, service and authentication logs.
controls.business_impact: Without journald most local logging stops and security events are lost.
controls.recommendation: Keep systemd-journald running.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask systemd-journald' and 'systemctl start systemd-journald'; journald is a static unit started on demand by its sockets.

controls.title: Ensure systemd-journal-remote service is not in use
controls.description: Checks that systemd-journal-remote.socket and .service are neither enabled nor active.
controls.rationale: A log client should send logs, not accept them from other hosts.
controls.business_impact: An active journal-remote listener accepts log data from the network, which can be abused to flood or forge logs.
controls.recommendation: Disable systemd-journal-remote on log clients.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl --now mask systemd-journal-remote.socket systemd-journal-remote.service'.

controls.title: Ensure journald is configured to send logs to rsyslog
controls.description: Checks that journald forwards to rsyslog (ForwardToSyslog=yes) and that rsyslog and journald are both active, when rsyslog is the logging method.
controls.rationale: rsyslog only receives journal messages when journald forwards them.
controls.business_impact: Without forwarding, events captured by journald never reach rsyslog files or remote collectors.
controls.recommendation: Configure journald to forward to rsyslog.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-cis.conf with '[Journal]' and 'ForwardToSyslog=yes', then 'systemctl reload-or-restart systemd-journald'.

controls.title: Ensure journald Storage is configured
controls.description: Checks that journald Storage is persistent.
controls.rationale: Persistent storage keeps logs across reboots.
controls.business_impact: Volatile logs are lost on reboot, which is often exactly when an investigator needs them.
controls.recommendation: Set journald Storage=persistent.
controls.remediation: Create /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-cis.conf with '[Journal]' and 'Storage=persistent', then 'systemctl reload-or-restart systemd-journald'.

controls.title: Ensure journald Compress is configured
controls.description: Checks that journald compresses large journal entries (Compress=yes).
controls.rationale: Compression keeps more history within the same disk budget.
controls.business_impact: Uncompressed journals fill their size limit sooner, shortening retained history.
controls.recommendation: Set journald Compress=yes.
controls.remediation: Add 'Compress=yes' under [Journal] in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-cis.conf and restart systemd-journald.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog is installed
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog is installed when it is the chosen logging method.
controls.rationale: rsyslog provides flexible local logging and remote forwarding.
controls.business_impact: If rsyslog is the logging design but is missing, logs are not written or forwarded as intended.
controls.recommendation: Install rsyslog.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install rsyslog'.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog service is enabled and active
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog.service is enabled and active.
controls.rationale: Logging only works while the daemon runs.
controls.business_impact: A stopped rsyslog silently drops logs and remote forwarding.
controls.recommendation: Enable and start rsyslog.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask rsyslog' and 'systemctl --now enable rsyslog'.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog log file creation mode is configured
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog sets $FileCreateMode to 0640 or more restrictive.
controls.rationale: Log files often contain sensitive operational and authentication data.
controls.business_impact: With the default mode 0644 any local user can read system logs.
controls.recommendation: Set $FileCreateMode 0640.
controls.remediation: Add '$FileCreateMode 0640' to /etc/rsyslog.d/60-cis.conf and restart rsyslog.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog is not configured to receive logs from a remote client
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog does not load the imtcp or imudp network input modules.
controls.rationale: Only designated log servers should accept logs from the network.
controls.business_impact: A listening rsyslog accepts spoofed log entries and can be flooded to exhaust disk space.
controls.recommendation: Disable network log reception on log clients.
controls.remediation: Remove imtcp/imudp module loads and inputs ($ModLoad imtcp, $InputTCPServerRun, module(load="imudp") and similar) from /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/, then restart rsyslog.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog-gnutls is installed
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog-gnutls is installed so rsyslog can use TLS.
controls.rationale: TLS protects forwarded logs in transit.
controls.business_impact: Without TLS support, forwarded logs travel in clear text and can be read or altered.
controls.recommendation: Install rsyslog-gnutls.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install rsyslog-gnutls'.

controls.title: Ensure rsyslog forwarding uses gtls
controls.description: Checks that rsyslog network streams use the gtls (TLS) stream driver.
controls.rationale: Log forwarding should be encrypted and authenticated.
controls.business_impact: Clear-text log forwarding lets an attacker read, drop or inject log entries on the network.
controls.recommendation: Use the gtls driver for rsyslog forwarding.
controls.remediation: Set StreamDriver="gtls" with StreamDriverMode="1" and an x509 authentication mode on forwarding actions in /etc/rsyslog.d/, then restart rsyslog.

controls.title: Ensure access to all logfiles has been configured
controls.description: Checks that every file under /var/log meets the CIS mode, owner and group rules for its type (for example 0640 root:adm for syslog files, 0664 root:utmp for wtmp).
controls.rationale: Log files contain security-relevant and sometimes sensitive data.
controls.business_impact: Over-permissive log files let local users read authentication records or tamper with evidence.
controls.recommendation: Restrict log file permissions and ownership.
controls.remediation: Correct the reported files with chmod/chown (for example 'chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx <file>') and fix the creating service or logrotate 'create' directive so new files keep those permissions.

controls.title: Ensure auditd packages are installed
controls.description: Checks that auditd and audispd-plugins are installed.
controls.rationale: The Linux audit framework records security-relevant events for accountability and forensics.
controls.business_impact: Without auditd, changes to users, permissions and security configuration are not recorded.
controls.recommendation: Install auditd and its dispatcher plugins.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install auditd audispd-plugins'.

controls.title: Ensure auditd service is enabled and active
controls.description: Checks that auditd.service is enabled and active.
controls.rationale: Audit rules only produce records while auditd runs.
controls.business_impact: A stopped auditd means security-relevant activity goes unrecorded.
controls.recommendation: Enable and start auditd.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask auditd' and 'systemctl --now enable auditd'.

controls.title: Ensure auditing for processes that start prior to auditd is enabled
controls.description: Checks that every GRUB kernel entry includes audit=1.
controls.rationale: audit=1 enables auditing before auditd starts, so early boot processes are audited.
controls.business_impact: Processes started before auditd would otherwise be unauditable, hiding early-boot persistence.
controls.recommendation: Enable auditing at boot.
controls.remediation: Add 'audit=1' to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub and run 'update-grub'.

notes.proxmox: On systemd-boot installs the kernel command line comes from /etc/kernel/cmdline; apply changes with 'proxmox-boot-tool refresh'.

controls.title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is configured
controls.description: Checks that every GRUB kernel entry sets audit_backlog_limit.
controls.rationale: A larger backlog prevents audit records from being lost during boot bursts.
controls.business_impact: With the default backlog of 64, audit events can be dropped before auditd starts.
controls.recommendation: Set audit_backlog_limit on the kernel command line.
controls.remediation: Add 'audit_backlog_limit=8192' to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub and run 'update-grub'.

notes.proxmox: On systemd-boot installs the kernel command line comes from /etc/kernel/cmdline; apply changes with 'proxmox-boot-tool refresh'.

controls.title: Ensure audit log storage size is configured
controls.description: Checks that max_log_file is explicitly set in /etc/audit/auditd.conf (the value is reported for review against site policy).
controls.rationale: Audit log size should be sized deliberately for the retention requirement.
controls.business_impact: Undersized audit logs rotate away evidence before it is collected.
controls.recommendation: Set max_log_file according to the retention policy.
controls.remediation: Set 'max_log_file = <MB>' in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and restart auditd.

controls.title: Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
controls.description: Checks that max_log_file_action is keep_logs.
controls.rationale: Audit logs should be rotated, never overwritten or deleted automatically.
controls.business_impact: Automatic deletion destroys audit evidence, which an attacker can trigger by generating noise.
controls.recommendation: Keep rotated audit logs.
controls.remediation: Set 'max_log_file_action = keep_logs' in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and restart auditd.

controls.title: Ensure system is disabled when audit logs are full
controls.description: Checks that disk_full_action is halt or single and disk_error_action is syslog, single or halt.
controls.rationale: The system must not continue unaudited when the audit disk is full or failing.
controls.business_impact: Continuing without auditing lets an attacker fill the disk and then act unrecorded.
controls.recommendation: Configure fail-safe actions for audit storage problems.
controls.remediation: Set 'disk_full_action = single' and 'disk_error_action = single' (or halt) in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and restart auditd.

controls.title: Ensure system warns when audit logs are low on space
controls.description: Checks that space_left_action is email, exec, single or halt and admin_space_left_action is single or halt.
controls.rationale: Administrators must be warned before audit storage runs out.
controls.business_impact: Without warnings the audit disk fills unnoticed and auditing stops or the system halts unexpectedly.
controls.recommendation: Configure low-space warnings and actions for auditd.
controls.remediation: Set 'space_left_action = email' (with a working MTA) and 'admin_space_left_action = single' in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and restart auditd.

controls.title: Ensure modification of the /etc/sudoers file is collected
controls.description: Checks that audit rules recording changes to /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d exist in /etc/audit/rules.d and in the loaded ruleset.
controls.rationale: Changes to sudo rules alter who can gain root.
controls.business_impact: Unrecorded sudoers changes can hide the creation of privileged backdoors.
controls.recommendation: Audit changes to /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d.
controls.remediation: Add to /etc/audit/rules.d/50-cis.rules: '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -F path=/etc/sudoers -F perm=wa -k scope' '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -F dir=/etc/sudoers.d -F perm=wa -k scope' Load the rules with 'augenrules --load' (a reboot is required when the audit configuration is immutable).

controls.title: Ensure actions as another user are always logged
controls.description: Checks that audit rules recording commands executed as another user (for example through sudo) exist in /etc/audit/rules.d and in the loaded ruleset.
controls.rationale: Commands run with a different effective user are privileged actions that need attribution.
controls.business_impact: Without these records, actions taken through sudo or setuid programs cannot be traced to the user.
controls.recommendation: Audit commands executed as another user (for example through sudo).
controls.remediation: Add to /etc/audit/rules.d/50-cis.rules: '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -C euid!=uid -F auid!=unset -S execve,execveat -k user_emulation' and the same rule with arch=b32. Load the rules with 'augenrules --load' (a reboot is required when the audit configuration is immutable).

controls.title: Ensure events that modify the sudo log file are collected
controls.description: Checks that audit rules recording changes to the sudo log file exist in /etc/audit/rules.d and in the loaded ruleset.
controls.rationale: The sudo log is evidence of privileged activity.
controls.business_impact: An attacker could edit the sudo log to hide their actions.
controls.recommendation: Audit changes to the sudo log file.
controls.remediation: Add to /etc/audit/rules.d/50-cis.rules: '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -F path=<sudo logfile> -F perm=wa -k sudo_log_file' (the path from Defaults logfile=). Load the rules with 'augenrules --load' (a reboot is required when the audit configuration is immutable).

controls.title: Ensure events that modify date and time information are collected
controls.description: Checks that audit rules recording changes to the system date, time and time zone exist in /etc/audit/rules.d and in the loaded ruleset.
controls.rationale: Time changes can disguise the sequence of events in logs.
controls.business_impact: An attacker could shift the clock to confuse log correlation and forensic timelines.
controls.recommendation: Audit changes to the system date, time and time zone.
controls.remediation: Add to /etc/audit/rules.d/50-cis.rules: '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S adjtimex,settimeofday -k time-change', '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S clock_settime -F a0=0x0 -k time-change' (both also for arch=b32) and '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -F path=/etc/localtime -F perm=wa -k time-change'. Load the rules with 'augenrules --load' (a reboot is required when the audit configuration is immutable).

controls.title: Ensure events that modify sethostname and setdomainname are collected
controls.description: Checks that audit rules recording changes to the host and domain name exist in /etc/audit/rules.d and in the loaded ruleset.
controls.rationale: The host identity is used in logs and network trust.
controls.business_impact: Renaming the host can mislead log correlation and monitoring.
controls.recommendation: Audit changes to the host and domain name.

controls.description: Checks that the audit tools are owned by root.
controls.rationale: Audit data, configuration and tools must be protected from tampering and disclosure.
controls.business_impact: Users who can read or change audit files can learn the monitoring policy, alter records or disable auditing.
controls.recommendation: Ensure the audit tools are owned by root.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules'.
