controls.title: Ensure AIDE is installed
controls.description: Checks that AIDE (aide and aide-common) is installed.
controls.rationale: File integrity monitoring detects unauthorized changes to system files.
controls.business_impact: Without integrity monitoring, replaced binaries and altered configuration can persist undetected.
controls.recommendation: Install AIDE and initialise its database.
controls.remediation: Run 'apt install aide aide-common' and 'aideinit', then move the new database into place as instructed.

controls.title: Ensure filesystem integrity is regularly checked
controls.description: Checks that dailyaidecheck.timer is enabled and active and that dailyaidecheck.service is static or enabled.
controls.rationale: Integrity checks only help if they run regularly.
controls.business_impact: Without scheduled checks, tampering is only found by chance.
controls.recommendation: Schedule daily AIDE checks.
controls.remediation: Run 'systemctl unmask dailyaidecheck.timer dailyaidecheck.service' and 'systemctl --now enable dailyaidecheck.timer'.

controls.title: Ensure cryptographic mechanisms are used to protect the integrity of audit tools
controls.description: Checks that AIDE monitors each audit tool with the p, i, n, u, g, s, b, acl, xattrs and sha512 attributes.
controls.rationale: Attackers who tamper with audit tools can hide their activity.
controls.business_impact: Replaced audit tools can silently drop or falsify audit records.
controls.recommendation: Protect the audit tools with AIDE.
controls.remediation: Add lines such as '/usr/sbin/auditctl p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512' for auditctl, auditd, ausearch, aureport and augenrules to /etc/aide/aide.conf.d/, then update the AIDE database.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/passwd is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/passwd is owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: /etc/passwd defines every local account.
controls.business_impact: A writable passwd file lets an attacker add accounts or change UIDs to gain root.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/passwd to root:root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/passwd' and 'chmod 0644 /etc/passwd'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/passwd- is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/passwd- is owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: /etc/passwd- is the backup of the account database.
controls.business_impact: A writable backup can be swapped in to restore attacker-controlled accounts.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/passwd- to root:root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/passwd-' and 'chmod 0644 /etc/passwd-'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/group is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/group is owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: /etc/group defines group membership.
controls.business_impact: A writable group file lets an attacker add themselves to privileged groups.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/group to root:root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/group' and 'chmod 0644 /etc/group'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/group- is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/group- is owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: /etc/group- is the backup of the group database.
controls.business_impact: A writable backup can be swapped in to restore attacker-controlled memberships.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/group- to root:root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/group-' and 'chmod 0644 /etc/group-'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/shadow is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/shadow is owned by root, group-owned by root or shadow, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: /etc/shadow holds password hashes.
controls.business_impact: Readable password hashes can be cracked offline to obtain passwords.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/shadow to root:shadow with mode 0640 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:shadow /etc/shadow' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/shadow'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/shadow- is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/shadow- is owned by root, group-owned by root or shadow, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: /etc/shadow- is the backup of the password hash database.
controls.business_impact: Readable backup hashes can be cracked offline just like the live file.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/shadow- to root:shadow with mode 0640 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:shadow /etc/shadow-' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/shadow-'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/gshadow is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/gshadow is owned by root, group-owned by root or shadow, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: /etc/gshadow holds group passwords and administrators.
controls.business_impact: Readable or writable group shadow data can expose or grant group privileges.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/gshadow to root:shadow with mode 0640 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:shadow /etc/gshadow' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/gshadow'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/gshadow- is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/gshadow- is owned by root, group-owned by root or shadow, and no more permissive than 0640.
controls.rationale: /etc/gshadow- is the backup of the group shadow database.
controls.business_impact: Readable or writable backup data can expose or grant group privileges.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/gshadow- to root:shadow with mode 0640 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:shadow /etc/gshadow-' and 'chmod 0640 /etc/gshadow-'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/shells is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/shells is owned by root, group-owned by root, and no more permissive than 0644.
controls.rationale: /etc/shells lists the valid login shells.
controls.business_impact: A writable shells file lets an attacker declare arbitrary programs as valid login shells.
controls.recommendation: Restrict /etc/shells to root:root with mode 0644 or stricter.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/shells' and 'chmod 0644 /etc/shells'.

controls.title: Ensure access to /etc/security/opasswd is configured
controls.description: Checks that /etc/security/opasswd and opasswd.old, if present, are root:root and no more permissive than 0600.
controls.rationale: These files store previous password hashes for reuse checks.
controls.business_impact: Readable old password hashes can be cracked and reveal patterns in users' current passwords.
controls.recommendation: Restrict the password history files to root with mode 0600.
controls.remediation: Run 'chown root:root /etc/security/opasswd*' and 'chmod 0600 /etc/security/opasswd*'.

controls.title: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured
controls.description: Checks local filesystems (excluding /run, /tmp, /var/tmp and container storage) for world-writable files and for world-writable directories without the sticky bit.
controls.rationale: Only directories designed for shared use should be world-writable, and they need the sticky bit.
controls.business_impact: Any user can modify world-writable files, which can lead to code execution or privilege escalation if privileged processes use them.
controls.recommendation: Remove world write access and set the sticky bit on shared directories.
controls.remediation: Run 'chmod o-w <file>' for each reported file and 'chmod a+t <directory>' (or remove o+w) for each reported directory.

controls.title: Ensure no files or directories without an owner and a group exist
controls.description: Checks local filesystems for files and directories whose owner or group does not exist.
controls.rationale: Orphaned files are typically left by deleted accounts or extracted archives.
controls.business_impact: A new account that reuses the orphaned UID or GID silently gains access to those files.
controls.recommendation: Assign orphaned files to a valid owner and group or remove them.
controls.remediation: Review each reported path and run 'chown <user>:<group> <path>' or delete it.

controls.title: Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords
controls.description: Checks that every account in /etc/passwd uses a shadowed password ('x').
controls.rationale: Password hashes must be kept in the root-only shadow file.
controls.business_impact: A hash left in world-readable /etc/passwd can be cracked offline by any user.
controls.recommendation: Move password hashes into /etc/shadow.
controls.remediation: Run 'pwconv' and investigate why the account was not shadowed.

controls.title: Ensure /etc/shadow password fields are not empty
controls.description: Checks that no account in /etc/shadow has an empty password field.
controls.rationale: Every account must require authentication or be locked.
controls.business_impact: An account with an empty password can be used without any credential.
controls.recommendation: Lock or set passwords for accounts with empty password fields.
controls.remediation: Run 'passwd -l <user>' for each reported account and investigate how the empty password was set.

controls.title: Ensure all groups in /etc/passwd exist in /etc/group
controls.description: Checks that every primary GID in /etc/passwd exists in /etc/group.
controls.rationale: Accounts should reference defined groups.
controls.business_impact: A later group created with the missing GID would silently gain those users' group access.
controls.recommendation: Correct primary groups that do not exist.
controls.remediation: Create the missing group or assign a valid primary group with 'usermod -g <group> <user>'.

controls.title: Ensure shadow group is empty
controls.description: Checks that the shadow group has no members and is no account's primary group.
controls.rationale: Members of the shadow group can read password hashes.
controls.business_impact: Accounts in the shadow group can read /etc/shadow and crack every password offline.
controls.recommendation: Remove all members from the shadow group.
controls.remediation: Run 'gpasswd -d <user> shadow' for members and change primary groups with 'usermod -g <group> <user>'.

controls.title: Ensure no duplicate UIDs exist
controls.description: Checks that no two accounts in /etc/passwd share a UID.
controls.rationale: Accounts sharing a UID are the same user to the kernel.
controls.business_impact: Actions cannot be attributed and one account silently has the other's access.
controls.recommendation: Give every account a unique UID.
controls.remediation: Assign unique UIDs with 'usermod -u <uid> <user>' and fix file ownership accordingly.

controls.title: Ensure no duplicate GIDs exist
controls.description: Checks that no two groups in /etc/group share a GID.
controls.rationale: Groups sharing a GID grant the same file access.
controls.business_impact: Members of one group silently receive the other group's access.
controls.recommendation: Give every group a unique GID.
controls.remediation: Assign unique GIDs with 'groupmod -g <gid> <group>' and fix file group ownership.

controls.title: Ensure no duplicate user names exist
controls.description: Checks that no user name appears twice in /etc/passwd.
controls.rationale: Duplicate names make authentication and auditing ambiguous.
controls.business_impact: The first matching entry wins, so a duplicate can shadow or impersonate an account.
controls.recommendation: Remove duplicate user names.
controls.remediation: Rename or remove the duplicate entries with 'usermod -l' or 'userdel'.

controls.title: Ensure no duplicate group names exist
controls.description: Checks that no group name appears twice in /etc/group.
controls.rationale: Duplicate group names make access control ambiguous.
controls.business_impact: Access decisions may use an unexpected GID for the group.
controls.recommendation: Remove duplicate group names.
controls.remediation: Rename or remove the duplicate entries with 'groupmod -n' or 'groupdel'.

controls.title: Ensure local interactive user home directories are configured
controls.description: Checks that each interactive user's home directory exists, is owned by that user and is mode 0750 or more restrictive.
controls.rationale: Home directories hold personal data, keys and shell startup files.
controls.business_impact: Other users could read private data or plant malicious startup files in accessible home directories.
controls.recommendation: Secure interactive users' home directories.
controls.remediation: Create missing homes with 'mkhomedir_helper <user>', then 'chown <user> <home>' and 'chmod 0750 <home>'.

controls.title: Ensure local interactive user dot files access is configured
controls.description: Checks interactive users' dot files: no .forward or .rhosts files, .netrc and .bash_history no more than 0600, other dot files no more than 0644, all owned by the user and the user's primary group.
controls.rationale: Dot files control shells, mail forwarding and stored credentials.
controls.business_impact: Writable startup files let others run code as the user; .rhosts and .netrc can grant or reveal access.
controls.recommendation: Secure or remove sensitive dot files in user homes.
controls.remediation: Remove .forward and .rhosts files, and run 'chmod go-w' (or 'chmod 0600' for .netrc and .bash_history) and 'chown <user>:<group>' on the reported files.

controls.title: Ensure local interactive user dot directories access is configured
controls.description: Checks interactive users' dot directories: .ssh no more than 0700, others no more than 0750, all owned by the user and the user's primary group.
controls.rationale: Dot directories hold SSH keys, application credentials and configuration.
controls.business_impact: Accessible dot directories expose private keys and tokens or allow others to plant configuration.
controls.recommendation: Secure dot directories in user homes.
controls.remediation: Run 'chmod 0700 <home>/.ssh', 'chmod g-w,o-rwx <dir>' for others and 'chown <user>:<group> <dir>' for the reported directories.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure unused filesystems kernel modules are not available
manual_recommendations.guidance: Review filesystem kernel modules that are loaded or loadable but not used by any mounted filesystem, and deny-list those without a business need.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Compare 'findmnt -Dkerno fstype', 'lsmod' and the modules under /usr/lib/modules/*/kernel/fs; add 'install <module> /bin/false' and 'blacklist <module>' entries for unused ones.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure the source.list and .source files use the Signed-By option
manual_recommendations.guidance: Verify that every deb/deb-src entry and deb822 stanza pins its repository to a dedicated keyring with Signed-By.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Add '[signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/<vendor>.gpg]' to .list entries or a 'Signed-By:' field to .sources stanzas, referencing a keyring for that repository only.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure updates, patches, and additional security software are installed
manual_recommendations.guidance: Verify that security updates and patches are applied according to the patch management policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Run 'apt update' followed by 'apt upgrade' (or your configuration management workflow) and reboot when a new kernel is installed.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure only approved services are listening on a network interface
manual_recommendations.guidance: Review every listening socket ('ss -plntu') and confirm each service is required and approved.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Stop, mask or remove services that are not approved, or restrict their listening addresses.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure IPv6 status is identified
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm whether IPv6 is required and record the decision; if it is not required disable it, otherwise configure it securely.
manual_recommendations.remediation: To disable IPv6 add 'ipv6.disable=1' to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX and run 'update-grub', or set net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1 and net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 = 1 in /etc/sysctl.d/.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure unneeded network protocol kernel modules are not available
manual_recommendations.guidance: Review network protocol modules that are loadable but unused and deny-list those without a business need.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Compare 'lsmod' with the modules under /usr/lib/modules/*/kernel/net and add 'install <module> /bin/false' and 'blacklist <module>' for unused protocols.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure sshd post-quantum cryptography key exchange algorithms are configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that post-quantum hybrid key exchange (mlkem768x25519-sha256 on OpenSSH 9.9+, and sntrup761x25519-sha512) is offered by sshd.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Include the post-quantum algorithms at the front of KexAlgorithms in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cis.conf and reload ssh.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure password complexity is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that password complexity (minclass and/or the dcredit, ucredit, lcredit and ocredit credits) follows site policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Set for example 'minclass = 3' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-cis.conf according to the password policy.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure minimum password days is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that PASS_MIN_DAYS and each account's minimum password age are greater than 0 in line with site policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Set 'PASS_MIN_DAYS 1' in /etc/login.defs and run 'chage --mindays 1 <user>' for existing accounts.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure journald log file access is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that journald log files under /var/log/journal and /run/log/journal have permissions that follow site policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Review systemd-tmpfiles rules for the journal (for example /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/systemd.conf) and override them in /etc/tmpfiles.d if needed.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure journald log file rotation is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that journald rotation (SystemMaxUse, SystemKeepFree, SystemMaxFileSize, MaxRetentionSec) follows site policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Set the rotation options in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-cis.conf and restart systemd-journald.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure rsyslog logging is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that rsyslog writes the required facilities and severities to appropriate log files.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Define the site's logging rules in /etc/rsyslog.d/ and restart rsyslog.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that rsyslog forwards logs to a central log host.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Add an omfwd action (for example action(type="omfwd" target="<loghost>" port="6514" protocol="tcp" ...)) to /etc/rsyslog.d/ and restart rsyslog.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure logrotate is configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that logrotate rotates and retains logs according to site policy.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Review /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d/ and adjust rotation frequency and retention.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure rsyslog CA certificates are configured
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that rsyslog TLS forwarding uses the site's CA certificate and verifies the log host.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Set DefaultNetstreamDriverCAFile and StreamDriverAuthMode=x509/name with the approved CA in /etc/rsyslog.d/.

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure the running and on disk configuration is the same
manual_recommendations.guidance: Confirm that the running audit rules match the rules on disk.
manual_recommendations.remediation: Run 'augenrules --check'; if a merge is needed, run 'augenrules --load' (reboot when the configuration is immutable).

manual_recommendations.title: Ensure SUID and SGID files are reviewed
manual_recommendations.guidance: Review the setuid and setgid programs on the system and confirm each is expected and approved.
manual_recommendations.remediation: List them with 'find / -xdev -type f -perm /6000' (the filesystem scan evidence also lists them) and remove the special bits from unapproved programs with 'chmod u-s,g-s <file>'.
